articles.title: Fantasy Football Fades: 3 big-name tight ends our analysts are avoiding at ADP in 2026 drafts
articles.summary: Proceed with caution on these TEs for 2026 fantasy football drafts.
articles.body:
The last position on our roundtable fades series for the week is tight end. Yahoo is also offering a new TE Premium format this season you can check out more details on here . The TE position can fall off fast if you're not too careful in your draft, though there are also plenty of opportunities to find gems in the later rounds. Today, analyst Scott Pianowski, Ray Garvin and Hayden Winks share the one tight end they're fading going into 2026 fantasy football drafts.

McBride will surely have a decent season, but my McBride fade is about the opportunity cost of selecting him. Most of my builds are going to be RB/WR focused in the early rounds, and I don't like falling one round behind in that RB/WR construction if I dip into the onesie markets too early. We also have to ask ourselves, what positions offer the most affordable options later in a draft? I feel good about the overall depth of the 2026 tight end board, which means I'm comfortable keeping those slots open (hopefully Juwan Johnson will be waiting for me).

Some regression is also likely for McBride this year. The Cardinals were absurdly pass-heavy after Jacoby Brissett took over last season, throwing at a pace of 685 pass attempts over a full schedule. That total would be the sixth-most all-time. Even if Arizona is a bad team again and playing catch-up most of the year, we have to realistically roll the attempts back. There's also some look-out-below potential with the Arizona offense later in the year, if third-round rookie QB Carson Beck is asked to start.

Perhaps the scariest part of McBride's profile is the new OC calling the plays – Nathaniel Hackett. The last three offenses run by Hackett have been horror shows, ranking 24th, 31st and 21st in yards and 24th, 29th and 32nd in points. Hackett had previous success tied to all-time great Aaron Rodgers in Green Bay, but it's been a mess ever since. It could be a long year in Arizona. — Scott Pianowski

Kittle is a soon-to-be 33-year-old who had Achilles surgery on Jan. 14. Week 2 will be exactly nine months from that point, and that's the absolute earliest we see skill players come back from it. Most of the time, there is a real ramp up period in terms of snaps, while efficiency also regresses. That's the part that is concerning for Kittle. Over the past two seasons, Kittle averaged 6.1 targets per game (TE8) and 10.7 yards per target (TE1). If the Achilles tear means he's closer to 5.0 targets per game (TE22) and 8.5 YPT (TE5), then he's only averaging 42.5 yards per game. That feels far more realistic than what a Round 7 price tag suggests. — Hayden Winks

Sam LaPorta exploded onto the scene as a rookie with 86 catches, 889 yards and 10 touchdowns in 17 games. Since then, though, it's been regression and now durability concerns are becoming part of the equation.

LaPorta played just nine games last season, finishing with 489 yards, three touchdowns and 11.9 fantasy points per game. Now he's already dealing with injuries heading into Week 1, which makes me even less interested in paying his current draft cost as the TE6 on Yahoo.

Detroit should still have one of the better offenses in football, but there are only so many opportunities to go around. Amon-Ra St. Brown is being drafted as a top-five wide receiver and Jahmyr Gibbs commands a massive role both as a runner and receiver. The law of conservation of targets has to kick in somewhere and I'm not convinced LaPorta gets enough volume to justify where he's being selected. This isn't about LaPorta being a bad player. At cost, I'd simply rather attack tight ends going later and invest that draft capital elsewhere. — Ray Garvin

articles.title: Mets lose to Astros despite strong start from Lindor and Soto
articles.summary: The offense was out-hit, and the bullpen could not keep things close during this rubber game loss.
articles.body:
The Mets struggled in multiple facets again in their loss to the Astros 6-3. Despite a decent outing from Zac Thornton, the Mets' bullpen could not hang on to the fragile lead they were given, and the offense had no response.

On his third pitch in the first inning, Thornton gave up a lead-off home run to Jeremy Peña. After striking out the next two hitters, Thornton allowed a single to Jose Altuve on a line drive into center field, but recovered when Christian Walker grounded into a force out for the third out. The Mets punched back quickly against Astros' rookie pitcher Ethan Pecko. Francisco Lindor led off with a home run on a full count, and Juan Soto followed with another dinger on the first pitch he saw. With no outs recorded, Bo Bichette smacked a ground ball into right field for a single. Unfortunately, the next three Mets batters went down in order to set the tone for the rest of the game. Nevertheless, after the first inning, the score was Mets 2, Astros 1.

With one out in the top of the second inning, Thornton hit Yainer Diaz with a pitch. After another out, Nick Allen bunted so softly that it took a minute for Marcus Semien to get to the ball and throw to first. By the time he did, Allen was safe, as was Diaz at second. Peña followed with an RBI single into center field that scored Diaz and moved Allen to third base. Fortunately, Yordan Alvarez flied out to mitigate the damage with the game tied. The Mets had no answers in the bottom of the inning, and the score remained 2-2.

Despite allowing a single to Walker at the top of the third, Thornton kept the Astros' hitters from scoring again. At the top of the fourth, the Astros' hitters continued to drive up Thornton's pitch count, and with two outs, Allen drove a double into the left-field corner. Peña came to the plate next, but fortunately this time he grounded out to Lindor at short. Thornton worked a 1-2-3 fifth inning, which was his last.

The Mets' offense was quiet for several innings until A.J. Ewing walked in the bottom of the fifth. He stole second base, and when Diaz's throw bounced past Peña, Ewing advanced to third as well. Marcus Semien walked to bring up Luis Torrens. Torrens grounded into a double play for the first two outs, but Ewing scored. Francisco Lindor grounded out to end the fifth inning, but the Mets were ahead 3-2.

Jonathan Pintaro replaced Thornton at the top of the sixth inning. After allowing a two-out double to right field from Diaz, Pintaro gave up a 2-run home run to pinch-hitter LaMonte Wade Jr, also in right field. Allen looped a single into center field after the homer to keep the rally going briefly, until Peña struck out to end the half. At the bottom of the sixth, Bichette smacked a double into center field for the Mets' first hit since the first inning. However, the Mets' lineup could not find any other momentum, and the inning ended with an Astros' lead, 4-3.

At the top of the seventh, Jefry Yan came in to pitch. After the first out, he issued a four-pitch walk to Isaac Paredes, then allowed a single to Altuve by deflecting a comebacker off his glove. Yan followed this up by hitting Walker with a pitch to load the bases. Daulton Varsho grounded out to first base, but Paredes scored on the play. Jared Young's subsequent throw to home was very wide, allowing Altuve and Walker to score as well. Diaz struck out for the third out, but the score was now Astros 6, Mets 3.

Austin Warren replaced Yan at the top of the eighth and retired the batters in order. With one out, Soto and Bichette both walked at the bottom of the eighth. The Astros opted to swap Bryan Abreu for Steven Okert, a lefty, on the mound at this point. The gambit worked when Okert retired Carson Benge to strand the runners and end the eighth-inning threat.

Chris Devenski pitched the ninth inning for the Mets and worked a 1-2-3 inning as well against his former team. After a delay to work on the mound, Josh Hader retired the first two batters he saw. Ewing doubled on a line drive to center field, but Semien flied out to end the game with an Astros win, 6-3.

The Mets travel to St. Petersburg to start a new series against the Tampa Bay Rays tomorrow. Robert Stock will face Ian Seymour, and first pitch is scheduled for 6:40 PM.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler wins second FedEx Cup title: Golf roundup
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler joined golf royalty as the third player to win multiple FedEx Cup championships.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — Scottie Scheffler has joined elite company.

Tiger Woods. Rory McIlroy. Scheffler. That's it. That's the list.

Scheffler joined golf royalty as the only players to win multiple FedEx Cup championships when he came from behind to capture the Tour Championship in the finale of the FedEx Cup playoffs Sunday, Aug. 30 at East Lake Golf Club.

Scheffler outdueled Norway's Viktor Hovland, who was also trying to join the multiple-Tour Championships club.

Scheffler, the world's No. 1 player and point standings leader, shot a 4-under-par 66 to finish 16-under 264, three shots ahead of Hovland. It was the second Tour Championship victory in three years for Scheffler, who won in 2024.

Hovland, the 2023 champion, couldn't hold a one-stroke lead heading into the final round. He shot 2-over to finish alone in second at 13 under.

McIlroy won the FedEx Cup three times (2016, 2019, 2022) and Woods twice (2007, 2009).

Scheffler overtook Woods for the top spot on the PGA Tour's career money list. With the $10 million first prize, Scheffler now stands at the top with $130,390,661. Woods held the top spot with $120,999,166.

Simply, Scheffler took the championship by matching the low round of the day.

Back and forth they battled, with Scheffler playing two groups ahead. Hovland, at 15 under, led Scheffler by three strokes going into the final round.

Scheffler started strong by hitting his tee shot on the par-3 second to two inches. The birdie moved him one and two strokes behind Ryan Gerard and Hovland, respectively, before the leaders even teed off. Scheffler then birdied the fourth to tie for the lead with Hovland at 14 under, after the first-round leader bogeyed his opening hole. Gerard double-bogeyed the opening hole to fall behind.

Scheffler bogeyed the seventh but birdied the eighth to move back to 14 under and tied with Hovland.

Hovland birdied the eighth to move back to 15 under and retake the solo lead. Scheffler birdied the 10th to force another tie, then made a 5-footer for birdie at the 13th to move to 16 under and take the solo lead for the first time. He gave the lead back with a bogey on the 14th after a drive in the rough.

Hovland dropped back behind Scheffler with a bogey on the 13th, also following a drive in the rough.

The lead was two after Scheffler birdied the 16th, from the fairway bunker, to return to 16 under.

While Scheffler was playing the 18th, Hovland bogeyed the 17th to fall three shots back. He overshot the green from 103 yards with a lob wedge. Scheffler parred the 18th, but at that point had the comfortable lead with one hole to play. Hovland went on to par the 18th.

No one else really challenged Scheffler and Hovland. Of the others in the final three pairings: Gerard shot 2-over 72 and finished third at 12 under. Adam Scott of Australia also shot 72 and finished 10 under, tied for 11th.

Chris Gotterup and Sweden's Ludvig Aberg each carded a 1-over 71 and finished tied for fourth at 11 under along with McIlroy (69).

They were joined by Englishman Alex Fitzpatrick (66), Jacob Bridgeman (68), Australian Min Woo Lee (68) and Russell Henley (68).

Scheffler moves closer to the Player of the Year award with his third win, including two in the playoffs, and 10 top-3 finishes.

Yin wins for first time since 2024 at FM Championship

China's Ruoning Yin fought off a challenge by South Korea's Hyo Joo Kim and captured the FM Championship by two strokes on at TPC Boston in Norton, Mass.

Yin, 23, carded a 2-under-par 70 and finished with a 14-under total of 274 to win for the sixth time on tour.

Kim, who grabbed the lead and got to 13 under by birdieing holes Nos. 7, 9 and 10, bogeyed the 16th hole and recorded a 1-under 71 to finish solo second at 12 under.

Allisen Corpuz (11 under) and Rose Zhang (10 under) tied for the low round of the day at 4-under 68. Corpuz, who was tied for the lead after two rounds, finished alone in third place, while Zhang tied for fourth with South Korea's Sei Young Kim (73).

Yin, Hyo Joo Kim and Sei Young Kim battled all day in the final group and each held a lead on the back nine.

Sei Young Kim chipped in for a birdie 2 on the par-3 11th to get to 14 under, but took a double-bogey 7 on the ensuing hole and two more bogeys on Nos. 13 and 14 to fall out of contention.

Yin rolled in a 25-foot birdie putt on the par-5 12th hole to tie Hyo Joo Kim at 13 under.

But Hyo Joo Kim suffered a three-putt bogey on the par-3 16th hole, misfiring from 9 feet away for par.

Both players parred No. 17 and Yin finished off her first win of the year with a birdie on the 72nd hole. Yin's last win occurred at the Maybank Championship in October 2024.

Top-ranked Nelly Korda shot a 1-over 73 and tied for 50th place at 1 over for the week.

Sweden's Anna Nordqvist wrapped up her final event on the LPGA Tour by tying for 38th at 1 under. The 39-year-old three-time major champion will captain the European team at the Solheim Cup next month.

articles.title: Steelers make rare decision with 4 QBs on 53-man roster for 2026
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers made the rare decision to carry four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The final roster cuts have arrived, which means there's no more speculating as to what the Pittsburgh Steelers will do with their quarterback room.

On NFL roster cutdown day, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Steelers indeed plan to keep four quarterbacks on their 53-man squad: Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard , and Drew Allar.

Four-man quarterback rooms are rare when it comes to 53-man rosters, which is why many assumed the loser of the QB2 battle between Rudolph and Howard would get a one-way ticket out of Pittsburgh. But the Steelers apparently erred on the side of caution, opting to keep two veterans and two young quarterbacks heading into the 2026 season.

Surprisingly enough, the Steelers aren't the only AFC North team to bring four quarterbacks onto their roster, as the Cleveland Browns are expected to keep Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel (IR), and rookie Taylen Green in their 2026 quarterback room.

With the Steelers set to keep four quarterbacks, other positions will unfortunately see their depth tested, as evidenced by the recent releases of fan-favorite linebacker Elandon Roberts and 32-year-old veteran defensive lineman Dean Lowry.

articles.title: Texans to place WR Tank Dell on injured reserve to begin 2026 season
articles.summary: WR Tank Dell addresses the media for the first time since his gruesome knee injury that caused him to miss the 2025 season.
articles.body:
Finally, the Houston Texans have revealed their plans for wide receiver Tank Dell headed into the 2026 NFL season.

According to multiple reports, the Texans have placed Dell on the injured reserve to begin the season. The speedster will miss the first four games of the season, but will be eligible to return Oct. 11 against the Tennessee Titans at Reliant Stadium.

Dell tore his ACL, MCL and LCL, along with dislocating his kneecap and suffering significant meniscus damage, which required multiple surgeries and forced him to miss the entire 2025 season while rehabbing. For 18 months, fans pondered if the former third-round pick would ever return to full form.

Fast-forward to this training camp and Dell was back at practice in a limited role.

As much as the physical recovery was challenging, Dell mentioned the internal struggle as a focal issue, too.

"I'll say mentally, it's just about trusting that the work you put in prior to going out there to do those things," Dell said avout his recovery last month. "Prior to going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me so that when I got out here I wasn't scared and I was talking to my doctor and I was just asking him questions and he was just telling me to let loose, trust it and be you because it's 100% stable. When he told me that, I just came out and was putting my foot in the ground. I didn't care about it, I tried not to think about it, because during your process the mental aspect of it is the hardest thing you have to get over. If I went out there iffy about what I'm doing, then I probably would never be able to come back to what I want to be. I was just out there, just trusting it, putting my foot in the ground, trying to be explosive and it's working in my favor."

Over his two active seasons with the Texans, Dell has caught 98 passes for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns. He's thankful for the team's patience and belief in his recovery, but he's now ready to be back after a short stint on IR.

Right now, the Texans only have five receivers on the active roster: Nico Collins, Jaylin Noel, Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson and Jared Wayne.

articles.title: Full list of Patriots moves at the NFL roster deadline
articles.summary: The Patriots made 42 total transactions ahead of the NFL roster cutdown deadline.
articles.body:
Coming out of their preseason finale and entering cutdown weekend, the New England Patriots had 91 players on their roster. Accordingly, they and their players were in for a few busy days: before Sunday's roster cutdown deadline, they needed to make at least 38 moves to get below the 53-player threshold mandated by the NFL.

In actuality, they made 42. The first 19 of those moves happened on Saturday, as did one that actually added a player to the mix . The rest — a total of 22 additional transitions, as charted by our Patriots roster cuts tracker — took place on Sunday.

The full list, split in different categories for easier digestion, looks as follows.

Players with less than four years of accrued experience are subject to waivers. This means that the following 31 will first have to pass through the waiver wire, where they might get claimed by any NFL team, before entering the open market.

The lion's share of cuts made over the weekend were of the waiver variety. As noted above, all of the players listed here are now subject to being claimed by other clubs before they could potentially return to the Patriots practice squad or, in the case of Jam Miller and Eric Butler, revert to injured reserve.

As for the list itself, it mostly includes depth players whose odds of making the 53-man roster were slim to begin with. The few names worth pointing out include running backs Lan Larison and Jam Miller, who are candidates to return should they clear waivers, as well as linebacker Chad Muma. Safety John Saunders Jr. also looked like a roster-worthy player but ultimately was made obsolete due to the trade acquisition of Jaylen Reed.

The following players were let go as vested veterans, meaning that the do not have to pass through waivers. They become free agents right away, meaning that they can sign with any team now.

The biggest surprise among the veterans being let go by the Patriots over the weekend was Kindle Vildor. The 2020 fifth-round draft choice, who joined the team in free agency this offseason, looked like a potential fifth cornerback at times during training camp. However, he ultimately was cut in favor of two rookies, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada.

Patriots players placed on reserve lists

The players listed here were all sent to reserve lists ahead of the roster cutdown deadline. All three of the names listed here are eligible to return.

Marcus Bryant will open the season on injured reserve with a designation to return. He will have to sit out at least the first four weeks of the regular season, as will Harold Landry and Brenden Schooler, whose statuses on the physically unable to perform and non-football injury/illness lists were changed from "active" to "reserve" on Sunday.

Not on this list yet are the aforementioned Jam Miller and Eric Butler, who were waived with an injury designation over the weekend. They will revert to New England's IR list once they make it through the waiver wire unclaimed.

While roster cuts made up the vast majority of moves this weekend, the Patriots also brought in some talent through the trade market.

The Patriots sent a 2028 seventh-round draft pick to the Cardinals to acquire Corey Kiner and did a late-round pick exchange with the Vikings to bring in Walter Rouse. Both moves are of the low-cost variety and effectively allow the team to jump the waiver wire: instead of waiting for Kiner or Rouse to remain unclaimed until it is their turn at No. 31, the Patriots secured their rights via trade.

The Tennessee Titans have announced their initial 53-man roster ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL season , though plenty is still subject to change.

The Titans trimmed their active roster down to 53 players from the 91 men it stood at throughout training camp on Aug. 30 in accordance with the NFL deadline. Most prominently, the Titans parted ways with quarterback Will Levis , a one-time starter who'd been groomed to be the Titans' quarterback of the future in 2023-24 before being benched and replaced. Other prominent players who didn't make the cut for the Titans include guard Cordell Volson, wide receiver K.J. Osborn and DE Malik Herring.

Just because the Titans are at 53 players now doesn't mean the roster is set in stone. The Titans still sit at No. 4 in the waiver order and can put in claims to pick up waiver-eligible players who were released on Aug. 30. articles.title: Bears finalize initial 53-man roster, cut LB Jack Sanborn, WR Kaden Davis: reactions
articles.summary: What you see today when it comes to the Bears’ 53-man roster will be different as soon as tomorrow. And it will change again. Then again and again … and...
articles.body:
What you see today when it comes to the Bears ' 53-man roster will be different as soon as tomorrow. And it will change again.

Things are always fluid with the construction of NFL rosters – especially when you're a young team like the Bears with a coaching staff entering its second season together.

With that said, there's still plenty you can glean from the team's initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season, whether it's certain strengths, glaring weaknesses or surprise decisions.

Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum

Adam Jahns: The Bears have one of the best young starters in the league, one of the best young backups in the league and one of the most experienced mentors in the league. Not bad at all. The Bears used to dream about QB rooms like they have right now under head coach Ben Johnson .

Mark Carman: One year ago things were "fra-gee-lay" between Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams behind the scenes. Now they are on the same track, being supported by Tyson Bagent, who many, including Ben Johnson, believe should be a starter in the league. Keeping Case Keenum around for his mentorship was a solid choice as well.

Greg Braggs Jr.: The starter is on the cover of Madden, Ben Johnson thinks the backup is a top-32 QB in the league and the third-string is better than the Vikings' starter. QB coach J.T. Barrett is probably better than half the QBs in my lifetime. What a room.

D'Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Roschon Johnson

Jahns: With a roster spot to secure, Johnson had arguably the best outing of his career against the Titans: 46 offensive snaps, 15 carries, 52 yards, a touchdown, two catches, 11 yards. He also excelled in pass protection. Rookie receiver Zavion Thomas doesn't get to show his speed on his 97-yard touchdown catch without Johnson sliding over to pick up a blitzer.

Patrick Norton : Johnson making the roster shouldn't come as a shock to anybody. He's a valuable special-teamer and well-liked within the locker room despite his lacking offensive contributions. Don't be surprised to see Salvon Ahmed brought back to the practice squad. He could get some action with a game-day elevation to the active roster if Kyle Monangai is unable to go in Week 1 after hyperextending his knee earlier in the preseason.

Carman: One of the key question marks the Bears have entering the season is the health of Monangai. There is a significant drop-off between Monangai and Johnson. Ben Johnson might have to rely on D'Andre Swift a little more than he would like in the early going. Swift has looked up to the task, primed for perhaps his best season yet vying for a new contract.

Braggs: If Colston Loveland didn't exist, D'Andre Swift would probably be the Camp MVP this year. He has looked really good. I would give my life for Kyle Monangai. But Roschon Johnson making this team surprised me. Was not expecting that. Hey, if you live up to the challenge put by Ben, that's all right by me.

Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, Zavion Thomas, Jahdae Walker

Adam Hoge: This is the most talent the Bears have had at wide receiver since the Brandon Marshall-Alshon Jeffery days, and this group probably has a higher overall ceiling. But it is a young group, so the continued development of Odunze, Burden, Thomas and Walker throughout the season will be interesting to watch. Raymond already has had a big impact as the veteran in the room, but how many catches will he actually have in the regular season?

Norton : It's not worth acting surprised for a few hours that Kaden Davis didn't make the initial roster. The shock would come if he isn't invited back to the practice squad — or even the active roster once safety Coby Bryant is placed on injured reserve.

Carman: Who will step up and take the No. 1 receiver spot? The gambling markets are betting on Burden, as is Burden, who is his usual confident self. Thomas had a stellar end to the preseason and Walker is likely to make a jump as well. Can Odunze stay healthy and be the guy the Bears drafted him to be?

Braggs: Burden is in for a monster year. But if anybody's selling stock on Odunze, I'll buy it. Raymond may end up being the most crucial pickup of the entire offseason if the clear mentorship he's shown this summer pays off the way I think it will. Walker continues to intrigue me with star potential. The dude is a psycho.

Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, Sam Roush, Hayden Large

Norton : Hayden Large was one of the UDFAs that ALLCITY draft expert Fran Duffy considered a challenger for the initial roster back in April. Versatile as a blocking threat out of the backfield, he's a piece Ben Johnson should enjoy deploying.

Carman: The biggest sure thing on the roster is this room. Loveland becoming the best tight end in football is on the table. He will get a chance to do it as Caleb seems more comfortable with him than anyone else. Roush is not ready yet, but it seems like he will contribute. Kmet is Mr. Reliable and deserves to play on a winner as much as anyone in the Bears locker room.

Braggs: Colston Loveland has a chance to be one of the best players in the NFL. End scene.

Tackles: Darnell Wright, Braxton Jones, Theo Benedet, Ozzy Trapilo

Interior: Joe Thuney, Jonah Jackson, Garrett Bradbury, Logan Jones, Luke Newman, Jordan McFadden

Hoge : The bad news is that the Bears' wide-open left tackle competition didn't really work, but the good news is that Jones – once again the winner by default – is healthier than he was a year ago when he struggled to get through full games. The even better news is that Trapilo is coming. I wouldn't be shocked if he gets involved in team drills this week.

Carman: It is now or never for Braxton Jones, who is getting an opportunity that very few thought he would get. It feels like the Bears are holding on for Ozzy Trapilo but when will that be? Jones seemed very confident in his return to play early in camp before getting hurt. How far did that set him back? Meanwhile, Bradbury was not pushed at all by Jones early, but Jones is at least starting to find his way.

Braggs: When Cole Kmet says the transition at center has been seamless from Drew Dalman to Bradbury, I believe him. That is the most important storyline for the offensive line this offseason, of which there were many. They proved last year they can maneuver around a murky left tackle situation, and that was last year with an offense less prepared. Not worried about that unit one bit. Pretty nice, huh?

Edge: Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Dayo Odeyingbo, Jamree Kromah, Daniel Hardy

Interior: Grady Jarrett, Kentavius Street, Neville Gallimore, Jordan van den Berg, Jayden Loving

Jahns : The Bears' decision to trade Gervon Dexter Sr. is rooted in the past and the future. He was drafted in the second round in 2023 to fill a role in former coach Matt Eberflus' defense – and he was in the final year of his contract. A second contract with the Bears was unlikely.

Dexter was a solid but not a sensational player. His role and importance appeared to be diminishing during training camp, though. Street and van den Berg started to rotate in with the first team weeks ago. It didn't stop, either.

Instead, Loving – an undrafted rookie – also started to impress more and more.

Hoge : This is a much better interior group than the Bears had last year, with a solid group of veterans mixed in with two rookies who are already outperforming their draft status.

But the outside pass rush remains eerily similar to last year, especially because Booker is dealing with an injury again.

Braggs: Ben Johnson is trying to sell me on the depth of the interior line. I'm still in wait-and-see mode. Let's see how they stop the run. Still have little belief they'll be able to get to the QB consistently. It's mostly the same unit as last year and they didn't upgrade. Is Jordan van den Berg the truth? We're about to find out. He was fun to watch at camp. Let's see how he handles a counterpunch from the NFL.

T.J. Edwards, Devin Bush, D'Marco Jackson, Keyshaun Elliott

Norton: If there's a group almost certain to look different before Week 1, it's this one. Maybe Jack Sanborn comes back after some post-cutdown roster maneuvering.

Braggs: Easily the least talked about unit on the Bears on either side of the ball and definitely the unit that should be talked about more. They appear to have quality depth. TJ Edwards looks healthy. D'Marco Jackson looks empowered. And Devin Bush looks like a heat-seeking missile at times.

Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad II, Clark Phillips III, Josh Blackwell

Jahns: Smith appeared to be making a late push after missing part of camp with an injury. It included making two pass breakups in the Bears' preseason win against the Titans.

But the arrival of Phillips changed Smith's place on the team. Phillips has the versatility to play outside at cornerback and inside at nickel back, where Muhammad appears to be the starter as a rookie right now.

Hoge : Phillips was primarily an undersized outside corner in Atlanta so it will be interesting to see if the Bears have different plans for him. It's a shame Smith couldn't stay healthy because he certainly showed starting potential when he was able to play. Don't forget about Cam Lewis. If something were to happen to Johnson or Stevenson, they could kick Muhammad outside and put Lewis in the slot.

Braggs: This unit is cursed, plain and simple. Murphy's Law: anything that can go wrong will go wrong. I had a close eye on Jaylon Johnson during camp. He was getting beat quite a bit from my eyes against a tough Bears offense but it sounds like he had good showings in the joint practices. I think we need to have reasonable expectations for rookies starting on this defense, including Malik Muhammed who's already been asked to do so many things at camp with all the injuries to that group.

Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis, Xavier Woods, Elijah Hicks, Coby Bryant, Skyler Thomas

Jahns: This feels like a position that changes often this season as the Bears try to make up for the loss of Bryant. That could mean the competition between Lewis, Woods and Hicks continues into the season. Or it could mean that other players are added to the mix.

Carman: Is Thieneman ready to be a No. 1 safety? Logic tells me no. At least he will have veteran leadership around him to help him progress. This is one of the weaker safety rooms in the league with Coby Bryant out.

Hoge : Where would this room be if Thieneman didn't fall to No. 25? The Bears really need him to be in the defensive rookie of the year conversation.

Braggs: I thought Thieneman finished camp strong. His play recognition started to speed up and he started to get in some windows. Next step? Trusting your eyes and taking away the football. I was hopeful Cam Lewis could be what Kalif Raymond is to the offense. And he could still be that, but with the injury to Bryant, it feels like he won't be able to thrive as a smaller role guy and now will be asked for bigger responsibilities.

Kicker Cairo Santos, punter Tory Taylor, long snapper Beau Gardner

Carman: Does Beau know long snapping? The Bears don't seem sold that he does. I don't think there is much room for error for the rookie. Taylor had an improved preseason. Will it translate? Santos distance seems to have gained a yard or three.

articles.title: Reds/Cubs Sunday Night Baseball game to begin in rain delay
articles.summary: It’s a tarp!
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Reds are set to wrap their weekend series in Wrigley Field against the Chicago Cubs on Sunday night. They're even going to have Joey Votto in the building as an on-field analyst seeing as the game is being carried nationally on both NBC and Peacock as the featured Sunday Night Baseball game of the week.

Unfortunately, it appears the game won't be starting on-time at 7:20 PM ET.

As veteran ESPN reporter Jesse Rogers relayed shortly after 6:40 PM ET, the game's going to be delayed due to rain in the Chicago area.

Just how long we'll have to wait before Shota Imanaga throws the game's first pitch remains to be seen.

What also becomes interesting is what impact this will have on Reds starter Chase Burns. He was already expected to begin seeing his total pitch counts reduced as a way of managing the load of getting through the entire season as a starter, and obviously having to stay warm for longer before even beginning the game could mean his already expected-to-be short night could end up even shorter.

articles.title: Seahawks 2026 roster cuts: Seattle waives both rookie cornerback draft picks
articles.summary: The Seahawks have waived Andre Fuller in addition to Michael Dansby.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have opted to keep neither of their seventh-round rookie cornerbacks on the initial 53-man roster.

ESPN's Brady Henderson reported that former Toledo corner Andre Fuller, who was drafted alongside former Arizona standout Michael Dansby, has been waived. Dansby was also waived by the team. If both clear waivers come Monday, then they could return via the practice squad.

Seattle's cornerback room post-Riq Woolen appears to be constantly fluctuating outside of Josh Jobe, Devon Witherspoon, and Nehemiah Pritchett. The team drafted Julian Neal in the third round, although he missed all of preseason with an injury, while Fuller and Dansby got extensive preseason work. Seattle also signed Terrion Arnold ( who likely won't be around any time soon ) and veteran Trevon Diggs, as well as traded for rookie cornerback Avery Smith from the Los Angeles Chargers . We shall see if another veteran corner in Noah Igbinoghene made the roster, or if he ends up getting released (and potentially put on the practice squad).

Unless Deven Eastern is an unexpected inclusion, none of Seattle's sixth- or seventh-rounders from this year's draft will have made the 53-man roster. It's not too much of a surprise given the perceived weakness of this year's draft as a whole.

articles.title: Evan Kung wins Bassmaster Elite at St. Lawrence River in a tournament for the record books
articles.summary: Evan Kung made a gutsy final-day gamble on the St. Lawrence River to overtake Trey McKinney and claim the Bassmaster Elite Series tournament title.
articles.body: What a finale to the 2026 Bassmaster Elite Series regular season. Nine different anglers crossed the 100-pound mark this week at the Bassmaster Elite at St. Lawrence River — the most Century Belts ever awarded at a single smallmouth event in Bassmaster history. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS And shockingly, that historic number almost wasn't even the most exciting thing that happened. Evan Kung made a furious final-day charge from behind to run down leader Trey McKinney and steal the tournament win right at the finish, capping a week in which he entered with his Elite Series career on the line. Kung sealed it with a final push on Championship Sunday Kung came into the St. Lawrence needing a strong finish just to keep his card in the Bassmaster Elite Series. Instead, he built a lead through four days of consistent fishing and closed it out with a Phoenix Boats Big Bass award (6 pounds, 13 ounces) on top of the tournament win. "It was a crazy week," Kung said. "I knew every day going in what I needed to catch just to stay in the Elites. Once I had that locked up, I went out today wanting the Century Belt. Once I had that, I just went looking for big ones." TENNESSEE ANGLER LANDS MONSTER 15-POUND LARGEMOUTH BASS THAT SHATTERS STATE RECORD HELD SINCE 2015 He described a gutsy final-day gamble that paid off: "I went to the lake for three hours, didn't catch a fish, came back in the river and caught that big one in the last 20 minutes. It was a crazy week." His pattern all week was simple and repeatable — about 95% drop shot, including several fish on a still-unreleased Great Lakes Finesse prototype bait. "It's coming out soon," Kung said. Kung entered the final day trailing McKinney's overnight lead of 83-5 by a pound and a half. He weighed in first among the two leaders and delivered a final-day bag of 27-12 — enough to vault him into the lead at 109-9 for the first time all week. That put the pressure squarely on McKinney, who needed 26-8 to answer and reclaim the win. He came up two pounds short, sealing the title for Kung in the tournament's final minutes. "It was a tough year on me, so it's great to end it like this," Kung said after the win. "I couldn't have thought of a better ending. I'm kind of at a loss for words right now." He thanked a support system that traveled with him all week — sponsors, friends, his mother, and his girlfriend's family. "It's extra special to have them all here to see it," he said. The entire Top 10 showed out on the St. Lawrence McKinney (2nd, 107-9) fell just short of the win but left Clayton with a much bigger prize waiting — Progressive Bassmaster Angler of the Year. Tucker Smith (3rd, 107-1) and Cory Johnston (4th, 106-7) both joined the Century Club with two of the heaviest four-day totals of their careers, finishing within a pound of one another. Cole Sands (5th, 105-10) delivered one of the week's best personal stories. The Tennessee pro spent a month and a half scouting the river ahead of the event and treated it almost like trout fishing. "I wanted one of those Century Belts so bad for so long, and I finally got one," Sands said. "And to get it with smallmouth at the St. Lawrence — this might be my favorite bass fishery on earth." On his approach: "I chose not to go to the lake — I saw in practice that the river had plenty of big smallmouth, and you just have to know how to read the current. It's almost like trout fishing, the way you have to drift your bait. I kept it real simple — a drop shot and a minnow bait — and it led to a great finish. No complaints." DENNY HAMLIN CHASES MONSTER LARGEMOUTH BASS IN TEXAS WITH BASSMASTER PRO CHRIS ZALDAIN Rounding out the Century Club: Brandon Cobb (6th, 103-14), JT Thompkins (7th, 103-0), Bryant Smith (8th, 101-3) and Fisher Anaya (9th, 100-5), who claimed his own belt on the final cast of a week that carried much bigger stakes for him (see below). Only Easton Fothergill (10th, 99-8) narrowly missed joining the club. This fishery lives up to the hype Nine Century Belts in a single weigh-in is proof that the St. Lawrence River is one of the best bass fishing spots in the country. Between the goby-fed smallmouth population and a stacked Elite Series field pushing each other all four days, this event will likely be remembered as one of the heaviest, most competitive smallmouth tournaments Bassmaster has ever run. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kung's name goes on the trophy. But on a leader board where 99 pounds wasn't even enough to crack the top nine, this was a win for the whole field — and for a river that delivered on every promise made about it heading into tournament week. Love all things fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram and TikTok!

articles.title: Curacao wins second Little League World Series in country's history, first since 2004
articles.summary: Curacao ended a 22-year title drought with an 11-2 rout of Nevada in the Little League World Series championship game on a dominant performance.
articles.body: A dream 22 years in the making has become a reality, as Curaçao has captured its first Little League World Series title since 2004. The tiny island nation of less than 200,000 citizens rode a dominant pitching performance and an offensive onslaught to an 11-2 victory over Nevada in the championship game. It was the second championship in the country's history, coming on the heels of their shutout victory over Japan in the International final. LITTLE LEAGUE WORLD SERIES SIGN-STEALING CONTROVERSY ERUPTS FOR THE SECOND STRAIGHT YEAR Nevada was looking for its first world championship after winning the U.S. title, and even took an early two-run lead in the second before Curacao would prove to be too much for The Silver State. Curaçao would immediately tie things up in the third before breaking the game wide open and scoring a combined nine runs in the subsequent three innings. STATE CHAMPIONSHIP HIGH SCHOOL BASEBALL GAME ENDS IN CHAOS AS PLAYER DOES SOMETHING RARE, BUT BEAUTIFUL The game wasn't without its drama, though, as Nevada had the bases loaded in the bottom of the sixth inning with a loud out to straightaway center field that carried to the warning track. If that ball flies a little further, perhaps the Curaçao players start to sweat a bit more, but even then, a five-run gap would likely have been too large a gulf to overcome for the American team. Long viewed as a Little League World Series powerhouse, Curaçao legitimized those claims by running roughshod through the entire tournament, and, in the process, becoming only the second team in LLBWS history to win a title with the country’s name on its uniform, joining Japan. Japan would claim a prize of their own in this tournament, taking Ohio down by a score of 4-2 to claim a victory in the consolation game. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Curaçao has been on a historic run with regard to international sports, as their soccer team also made it to the FIFA World Cup for the first time in program history and even recorded a point in the group stage. Congratulations to these young men for seeing their hard work come to fruition.

articles.title: 'Praggnanandhaa is No. 1 in the world': Viswanathan Anand after India's first Grand Chess Tour title | Exclusive
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: You remember the photo that made rounds on social media last April, just after Vaishali Rameshbabu, Praggnanandhaa's elder sister, had land.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: You remember the photo that made rounds on social media last April, just after Vaishali Rameshbabu, Praggnanandhaa's elder sister, had landed at the Chennai airport with the Women's Candidates medal wrapped around her neck. It was a photo of her family.Praggnanandhaa was there too, his facial gesture mirroring anything but the sorrow of an underwhelming campaign in the open category of the Candidates, his hand holding a placard congratulating his sister on her homecoming.If that was Vaishali's moment, Praggnanandhaa's is now.Late Thursday in St Louis, he beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13 to win the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals, becoming the first Indian and only the seventh player in the tournament's 11-year history to do it.The prize money was $200,000. But even more than the prize money, it is about a 21-year-old who somewhat imploded at the 2026 Candidates and now sits, by one of the sport's most respected judges, at the top of the world.During an interaction with TimesofIndia.com, Viswanathan Anand, who is set to return to the board with Alaskan Knights for the new season of the Global Chess League (GCL) this September, assessed Praggnanandhaa's turnaround since that Candidates low."During the Candidates, he was having a kind of slump," the former five-time World Chess Champion said. "His play had already started to decline at the end of last year, compared to the first half, but in the Candidates, it was really not very impressive. And then I thought he must have been a bit gloomy."I think at the moment, I would say he (Pragg) is the number one player in the world.What followed, in Anand's telling, was something closer to a pattern than a one-off recovery."In Norway Chess, he was not doing well. At some point, there were four rounds left, and he was in the bottom. And then he won four games in a row," Anand explained. "He did something similar here, though his performance was much better in Grand Chess Tour and also in the Rapid. He won the Rapid, did well enough in the Blitz to win the tournament. Then he was sort of competing for first place here."It's the shape of these comebacks that Anand keeps returning to. "He has this capacity, and it's becoming more and more noticeable that he's able to win late games and change everything," he remarked. "And that's a very, very rare skill and useful skill to have."Then came the line that will follow Praggnanandhaa into the Olympiad next month. "I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world," Anand told this website with utmost authority."Well, Magnus doesn't compete in the same events, but nonetheless, you know, if you take classical included, and I know Pragg, in the tournaments which happened in August and all, he performed incredibly well. If you go back to Norway Chess and then see the development from there, I think it's just fantastic."It's not an idle comparison. Praggnanandhaa's road to St Louis ran through 27 rapid and blitz games, nine classical games, and 16 more across the semifinals and final. He arrived having already beaten Magnus Carlsen twice in classical chess in Norway earlier this year, including a stretch of four straight classical wins to close out Oslo.In the GCT final itself, he lost the opening classical game to Caruana and fumbled a likely equaliser in the second before finding his footing, winning both rapid games to seize control, then holding the four-game blitz section to a 4-4 draw to close it out.He'd already avenged a bruising from World Championship Challenger Javokhir Sindarov, who beat him twice at the Cyprus Candidates, by finishing joint-first with him at the Sinquefield Cup.ALSO READ: Praggnanandhaa’s invisible second: The making of Vaibhav SuriHe'd been beaten there by Vincent Keymer, too, before eliminating the German in the GCT semifinal.For a player whose technical range and universal style have long had experts rating him the most complete of India's young elite, the Candidates collapse had looked like the one gap in the resume. PETE CROW-ARMSTRONG GETS INTO UGLY, CURSE-FILLED SCREAMING MATCH WITH FEMALE WHITE SOX FAN As Colorado clung to a 1-0 lead, Carrigg dove for Michael Harris II's fly ball but came up empty. articles.title: Djokovic crashes out of US Open in five-set defeat to Navone
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic crashed out in the first round of the US Open after a five-set, near five-hour ordeal during which he was repeatedly sick on court. The 39-yea...
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic crashed out in the first round of the US Open after a five-set, near five-hour ordeal during which he was repeatedly sick on court.

The 39-year-old looked physically spent throughout the match and was regularly doubled over in pain, but still took Argentina's Mariano Navone the distance.

Djokovic swallowed pills and used an inhaler after vomiting at least three times, but despite being in obvious discomfort, he refused to throw in the towel.

However, the 24-time grand slam champion could not prevent a 7-6 (7-5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 defeat and first exit in the opening round of a major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.

The last time the Serbian great had been seen on a tennis court, in Cincinnati two weeks ago, he was collapsing to his knees and being sick into a towel.

After that defeat by Thiago Tirante, Djokovic revealed he had a "health issue" which he has been dealing with "for many years," and which affects him in heat and humidity.

It was certainly warm in New York but by no means Cincinnati levels, yet Djokovic's cheeks were already red and his hair drenched in sweat midway through the first set, which he had led 3-0 but lost in a tie-break.

Having already successfully lobbied to have the roof closed, and with it the air conditioning switched on, Djokovic hit back late in the second set - after throwing up by the courtside towel box - with the crucial break for 6-5.

He was sick again midway through the third but still took his one chance to break serve, and vomited again at the start of the fourth before breaking once more for 2-1.

However, by now Djokovic appeared to be cramping up and he could barely move as Navone struck back, winning just one more game in a dramatic defeat over four hours and 36 gruelling minutes.

articles.title: Chargers 53-Man Roster: biggest surprises, strengths & remaining questions
articles.summary: The Sporting Tribune's Fernando Ramirez writes how the Chargers initial 53-man roster looks on cut down day.
articles.body:
El SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The Chargers cut their roster down to 53 players with some surprises and added twists. This is one of the deeper squads they have had in recent memory.

Here is a full breakdown of the initial 53-man roster. Remember, the Chargers can still add players through the waiver wire.

Quarterbacks (2) : Justin Herbert, Trey Lance

The Chargers need to look for another backup quarterback. Lance didn't have a strong training camp or preseason, so the team should explore other options behind Herbert.

Running backs (3) : Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal

No surprise here. Mitchell has missed some practice time, but the fact that he wasn't placed on IR means the team is confident in his availability moving forward.

Tight ends/Fullback (4) : Oronde Gadsden, David Njoku, Charlie Kolar, Alec Ingold

This is the strongest this group has looked on paper since maybe the Antonio Gates and Hunter Henry years. All three tight ends could make an impact, plus look for Ingold to consistently make plays in this offense.

David Njoku #83 of the Los Angeles Chargers participates in drills during training camp at The Bolt on August 9, 2026 in El Segundo, California.

Wide receivers (6): Derius Davis, Tre' Harris, Quentin Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Ladd McConkey, Brenen Thompson

Youth and speed are the best ways to describe this group, especially when Johnston and Davis are considered the veterans of the room.

The Chargers need their punt and kick returner, Davis, to make an impact because they have missed the threat he brings to special teams. McConkey is going to feast in this offense.

Offensive line (11): Joe Alt, Kayode Awosika, Travis Burke, Alex Harkey, Trevor Penning, Trey Pipkins III, Rashawn Slater, Jake Slaughter, Jacob Spomer, Cole Strange, Logan Taylor

They kept a lot of offensive linemen. The thought here is that one will most likely be the sacrifice when Branson Taylor returns from IR in four weeks. Also, if they claim players off waivers, one of these linemen could be on the way out.

Overall, this offensive line will go as Alt, Slater and Slaughter go.

Defensive line (5): Nick Barrett, Jamaree Caldwell, Justin Eboigbe, Teair Tart, Dalvin Tomlinson

This is an underrated group. Tomlinson, Tart and Eboigbe have been dangerous throughout training camp. This unit could be a major strength of the defense, especially when combined with the Chargers' edge rushers.

Jamaree Caldwell #99 of the Los Angeles Chargers in a defensive stance during practice of the team's training camp at The Bolt on July 26, 2025 in El Segundo, California.

Edge rushers (4): Bud Dupree, Khalil Mack, Akheem Mesidor, Tuli Tuipulotu

Mack has looked very, very strong throughout training camp and in the joint practice. He may have found the fountain of youth.

Tuipulotu is looking for a contract extension, so expect a big year from him. Mesidor adds a different element that could be exactly what this group needs.

Thirty combined sacks between these four? Take the over.

Linebackers (5): Troy Dye, Daiyan Henley, Del'Shawn Phillips, Denzel Perryman, Marlowe Wax

This is the same group that made the roster last season. Dye can step in for Perryman if needed, while Phillips is a key special teams contributor.

Wax has grown a lot since last season and could make a push for more playing time at linebacker.

Cornerbacks (5): Cam Hart, Donte Jackson, Deane Leonard, Rodney Shelley, Tarheeb Still

This group feels like it is missing something. Maybe undrafted free agent Rodney Shelley out of Georgia Tech is the answer, but the Chargers could make a trade for a veteran cornerback.

Especially considering Benjamin St-Juste was in the mix last season, adding another veteran wouldn't be surprising. Leonard is also a valuable gunner on special teams.

LA Chargers Rodney Shelley (24) participates in drills during Chargers training camp at USD on .Tuesday August 4, 2026 in San Diego, California.

Safeties (6): Derwin James, Tony Jefferson, RJ Mickens, Elijah Molden, Genesis Smith, Kendall Williamson

Chargers fans were not happy when a tweet was sent out saying Jefferson had been released, but it was later revealed that he had made the 53-man roster.

Jefferson is an impact player who has earned his role on this defense. Williamson is a key special teams contributor, while Mickens and Smith could compete to avoid being the inactive safety on game days.

Special teams (2): K Cameron Dicker, LS Josh Harris

The surprise move was the Chargers cutting punter JK Scott. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that the team made the move so it wouldn't risk another player being claimed.

The Chargers should still consider moving on and finding a better option at punter. Scott had two examples during the preseason in which things didn't work out for the team, and it might be time to explore an upgrade.

articles.title: Rams news: Aaron Donald sounds off on wife's role in stunning NFL comeback
articles.summary: For months, Aaron Donald teased his comeback with the Los Angeles Rams after retiring in 2024. Fans incessantly urged him to return, especially after the Ram...
articles.body:
For months, Aaron Donald teased his comeback with the Los Angeles Rams after retiring in 2024. Fans incessantly urged him to return, especially after the Rams acquired Myles Garrett in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in June.

They got their wish. On Sunday, Donald signed a one-year, $20 million contract with the Rams. In his announcement, he referenced Michael Jordan's famous two-word statement when the latter returned to the NBA in 1995: "I'm back."

But before getting the nod from the Rams, he asked the person at the very top of the hierarchy: His wife, Erica Donald. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year said he had long conversations with her, who was fully supportive .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I think my wife played a huge part in this, me making this decision period because if the wife wasn't happy, it wasn't going to get done right," said Donald in his media conference.

"You got to make sure that the household was good, the kid was okay with it all. Having those hard conversations, figuring things out, what I wanted to do if I was told to do it, how would we do it. My wife was on board. She said, if you want to do this, she's with me 100%."

As they say, behind every successful man is a woman.

Donald will play in his 11th season. He walked away in 2024 to focus more on his family, adding that he had nothing else to prove in the NFL. He helped the Rams win the Super Bowl in 2022. He is an eight-time All-Pro First Team member and a 10-time Pro Bowler.

He and Garrett will form a lethal one-two defensive punch, although Donald will have to get his feet under him after a long hiatus.

The Rams will face the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

articles.title: Cubs news: Craig Counsell makes Shota Imanaga's job status clear after loss to Reds
articles.summary: Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell made it clear that Shota Imanaga’s position in the starting rotation is not currently in danger after the left-hander was...
articles.body:
Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell made it clear that Shota Imanaga's position in the starting rotation is not currently in danger after the left-hander was out of sorts in Sunday night's 7-5 loss to the Cincinnati Reds.

Imanaga surrendered six runs on eight hits across five innings, taking his season record to 8-10 with a 4.01 ERA. The right stretch of the outing turned difficult after he completed three scoreless innings. Hector Rodriguez then launched a three-run homer in the fourth inning to give Cincinnati a 3-2 advantage.

The Reds added three more runs in the fifth. Dane Myers opened the inning with a home run against Imanaga, and Tyler Stephenson followed Elly De La Cruz's single with a two-run homer. Imanaga's velocity had diminished during the fifth inning, when Cincinnati extended its lead to 6-3.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Despite the difficult outing, Counsell said Imanaga's job is not in jeopardy at the moment, per ESPN's Jesse Rogers. The team instead wants to help the pitcher get back to his best. With rosters expanding, Chicago could consider giving Imanaga additional rest.

As things stand, Imanaga is scheduled to face the Miami Marlins on Saturday.

The loss came after the Cubs had defeated Cincinnati 17-5 on Saturday. The Reds entered Sunday having lost six of their previous seven matchups with Chicago, but Cincinnati secured the series finale behind three home runs and an excellent performance from rookie Sal Stewart, who hit his 31st homer of the season.

Pete Crow-Armstrong supplied two home runs for the Cubs , including his 38th of the season, but Emilio Pagan recorded his 19th save after allowing the ninth-inning solo shot.

articles.title: Rashid Latif slams Mohsin Naqvi's PCB as 'worst cricket board in 70 years' after Pakistan's horror Test series defeat in England
articles.summary: Rashid Latif has slammed PCB by calling it the “worst cricket board in 70 years” after Pakistan's disastrous Test series defeat in England.
articles.body:
Former Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Rashid Latif has launched a scathing attack on the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) following the team's Test series defeat in England .

Pakistan under Babar Azam lost the three-match series after going 0-2 after Leeds and Lord's Tests.

Latif said the focus should not only be on Pakistan team being labelled the "worst touring team in 50 years" but also on what he described as the "worst cricket board in the last 70 years."

Rashid Latif slams Mohsin Naqvi's PCB as Pakistan's England tour turns into a nightmare

Former Pakistan wicket-keeper Rashid Latif has launched a scathing attack on the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) and its chairman Mohsin Naqvi following the national team's disastrous Test series defeat in England

Latif argued that the players should not be the only ones facing criticism. Pakistan's performances have been so poor that the current side has reportedly been described by sections of the British media as the country's "worst touring team in the last 50 years."

Latif agreed that Pakistan's performances on the field have been unacceptable, but he also insisted that the criticism should also extend to the administration, selection committee, and coaching staff.

Speaking on Geo News , Latif said that while everyone was discussing the team's failures, not enough attention was being paid to the people responsible for running Pakistan cricket.

"Everyone is talking about the Pakistan team, and how it is the worst touring team in the last 50 years. But nobody is speaking about how the current board is the worst in the last 70 years."

"Nobody is talking about the worst selection committee and coaches," he added.

The former Pakistan captain opined that the team's decline has to be viewed as the result of problems throughout the system, including administration, selection and coaching.

"If you combine these issues, you will get the answer to your question," Latif said.

"You will know who has ruined this team. Now you are losing consistently. This is the worst cricket board, that's a fact."

The debate surrounding Pakistan's struggles has largely focused on the players and their repeated batting failures. Latif, however, believes the people making the decisions behind the scenes must also be held accountable.

Pakistan's batting horror against England adds to pressure with Babar Azam's failures

Pakistan's struggles in England have been particularly severe with the bat. The visitors are yet to cross the 200-run mark in an innings during the series against the English attack.

At Lord's, Pakistan were bowled out for just 110 in their first innings after England posted 290. The visitors showed greater resistance in the second innings while chasing a target of 388, but another early collapse left them handed them a 194-run defeat.

England have won the series with a 2-0 lead. As a consequence, players such as Imam-ul-Haq and Mohammad Rizwan have been sent home while white-ball coach Mike Hesson is set to take charge for the final Test with red-ball coach Sarfaraz Ahmed likely to be sacked, per Geo News.

The third and final Test match is scheduled for September 9 at Edgbaston, Birmingham.

articles.title: 76ers news: Jaylen Brown declares he's out for 'blood' in Year 1 with Philly
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown is entering his first season with the Philadelphia 76ers with something to prove. After spending the first 10 years of his NBA career with the...
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown is entering his first season with the Philadelphia 76ers with something to prove. After spending the first 10 years of his NBA career with the Boston Celtics, Brown was shockingly traded to Philadelphia this offseason in a blockbuster deal centered around Paul George and draft compensation. The move sent him from one Eastern Conference contender to another, but it also placed him on the other side of one of the NBA's biggest rivalries.

Now, Brown appears ready to embrace the opportunity with an aggressive mindset. In his recent Twitch livestream , the 29-year-old All-Star made his intentions clear when discussing his mentality heading into the upcoming season.

"I'll be listening, I'll be waiting, but my mentality is kill," Brown said. "I feel like I want blood this year. You know what I mean? Like I feel like that's the mentality. I want blood."

Brown's comments come after a turbulent offseason that ultimately led to his departure from Boston . The Celtics had reportedly explored trade possibilities involving their longtime star , including discussions surrounding a potential deal for Giannis Antetokounmpo. Brown previously expressed frustration with how the organization handled the situation , saying he felt a lack of respect throughout the process.

His move to Philadelphia gives him a chance to turn that frustration into motivation.

The timing also makes Brown's arrival in Philly particularly intriguing. The 76ers eliminated the Celtics in seven games during the first round of the 2026 playoffs after overcoming a 3-1 deficit. Brown was on the opposite side of that comeback, and he will now join the team that ended Boston's season.

Philadelphia's ambitions also extend beyond simply getting past the Celtics. The 76ers have assembled one of the league's most talented rosters , with Brown joining Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid. The team also added LeBron James, giving Philadelphia another veteran superstar with championship experience.

Brown is coming off one of the strongest seasons of his career. He averaged 28.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists while helping Boston win 56 games and secure the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference. He also finished sixth in MVP voting.

With a new team, a new supporting cast and plenty of motivation, Brown appears ready to make his first season in Philadelphia count. And if his latest comments are any indication, the new Sixers star isn't planning on taking it easy.

articles.title: Alejandra Salazar: "Sería precioso ganar mi último Mundial al lado de Gemma Triay"
articles.standfirst: La jugadora, que cuelga la pala a final de año, visita MARCA antes de encarar el último torneo de su vida en la ciudad que le vio crecer
articles.summary: La jugadora, que cuelga la pala a final de año, visita MARCA antes de encarar el último torneo de su vida en la ciudad que le vio crecer
articles.body: Es una semana especial. En muchos sentidos. Para ella, si cabe, todavía más. Alejandra Salazar Bengoechea (Madrid, 1985) tacha ya días del calendario antes de colgar la pala definitivamente tras 26 años de exitosa carrera. Un camino que va dejando el rastro de las despedidas y que esta semana, en el Movistar Arena, vendrá plagado de emociones en la que es su casa. Por ello, y tras anunciar hace poco más de un año en MARCA que 2026 sería su último baile, Salazar ha querido expresar sus emociones en este diario visitando la redacción antes de afrontar una semana que apunta a ser inolvidable para ella. P. ¿Cómo estás, Alejandra? R. Pues muy bien. De vuelta ya de unos días de cambio de rutina, de vacaciones y, nada, afrontando el último rush final de la temporada. P. Hace justo un año, un poquito más, viniste aquí y nos contaste que 2026 iba a ser el último año que jugarías como profesional. ¿Ha sido lo que te esperabas, dentro de que todavía no ha acabado, o te has encontrado por el camino sensaciones diferentes a las que esperabas? R. No venía con unas expectativas reales de sensaciones. He intentado fluir y ver lo que fuera pasando, evidentemente trabajándolo también a nivel emocional con un profesional y, bueno, dejándome llevar, queriendo dar lo mejor de mí en cada torneo y siguiendo con mis rutinas diarias para dar lo mejor en la pista. P. Es complicado eso de dejarse llevar a nivel emocional y seguir focus en lo que tienes que hacer dentro de la pista. ¿Cómo se lleva eso? Porque entiendo que es una sensación que obviamente no has experimentado a lo largo de tu carrera. R. Es verdad que hay torneos en los que has tenido más recorrido y que son más especiales y, a lo mejor, ha costado un poquito más, porque despedirte en lo que llevamos de año de algunos de ellos se ha hecho más especial o más emotivo. Pero en otros, al ser a lo mejor torneos nuevos, donde hay menos apego y donde tienes menos recuerdos, se han pasado, entre comillas, más fáciles o, en ese sentido, más neutros. P. Sí, porque entiendo que también puede llegar a pesar, en ciertos momentos, que te dé la sensación de una despedida constante, torneo a torneo. Sobre todo en esos torneos con más tradición, en ciudades e incluso países en los que has estado más a lo largo de los años. No sé si eso te ha llegado a costar en algunos momentos, decir: «Da la sensación de que es una despedida constante». R. Claro. Por eso no quería que en cada torneo me hiciesen, si acaso... Bueno, algunos han tenido detalles, a lo mejor más en privado, algún regalo o algo para que me acuerde de ellos, y se lo agradezco enormemente. Pero estar semana tras semana con eso en la cabeza creo que tampoco es necesario, ni tampoco me iba a venir bien a nivel emocional para estar enfocada en lo que de verdad quiero estar enfocada. Y cuando tenga que ser la despedida, pues será. P. ¿Qué es lo bonito que te estás llevando de esta etapa? R. Sí, al final la gente es más consciente de que son mis últimos partidos, de que son las últimas veces que me van a ver jugar a nivel profesional. Pero bueno, que no me voy. O sea, yo tengo muy claro que voy a seguir en este mundo, que voy a seguir compitiendo, a lo mejor a nivel de veteranos en un futuro, o ya se verá, pero que voy a seguir muy ligada. Entonces quizá yo no me lo tomo como una despedida. Es como si yo me siguiese viendo que voy a seguir aquí. Para la gente, pues bueno, he tenido muchos momentos muy bonitos, como dices, de gente que no quiere perder la oportunidad de acercarse y decirme alguna cosa bonita o alguna sensación que ha tenido cuando me ha visto jugar. Al final, es eso: momentos muy especiales que me llevo y todo ese calor que me llevan dando más de 20 años, pues este año es un poquito más concentrado. P. ¿Has descubierto una Alejandra que no conocías, más a nivel emocional, con todas estas nuevas sensaciones que se te están viniendo encima? R. Sí, desde luego. Creo que son sensaciones diferentes: cómo lo llevas, las actitudes que tienes cuando pasa una cosa u otra... Entonces es bonito también, porque te sigues conociendo a ti misma. P. ¿En qué ha cambiado la Alejandra que se sentó aquí hace un año, emocionada, diciendo que se iba a retirar a finales de 2026, y la Alejandra de ahora, que encara sus últimos meses? R. Pues... qué te digo. Yo me veo bastante parecida, pero quizá, a nivel todavía de madurez y de vivir esas experiencias últimas, pues bueno, un poquito más madura. P. ¿Se te ha llegado a pasar por la cabeza que igual te estás retirando pronto y que podrías haber seguido un poco más? R. Sí, lo tengo claro. Es una pregunta que me están haciendo frecuentemente. Al final, cuando sigues a buen nivel y sigues ahí, pues la gente te anima, te dicen que por qué no juegas un año más, que estás para más... Y bueno, es fenomenal que me vean así y lo agradezco muchísimo, pero a todos les digo lo mismo: que ya está, que lo tengo muy claro y que es mejor retirarme a muy buen nivel y sintiéndome súper competitiva, peleando cada partido. P. Con esto se me viene ahora a la cabeza una frase que me dijo Bela también antes de retirarse: Tengo la suerte de que el deporte no me ha retirado a mí. Porque, por desgracia, hay muchos jugadores y muchas jugadoras que, sobre todo por lesiones, han tenido que dejarlo porque ya físicamente no les daba más. R. Súper, súper convencida. Y, como dices, yo creo que es el privilegio de cualquier deportista el poder decidir cuándo retirarte, cómo retirarte y que no sea una lesión o una enfermedad la que lo haga por ti. Así que nada, ojalá estos meses que quedan las lesiones me respeten y pueda cumplir el objetivo de llegar hasta final de año. P. Objetivo Tour Finals, ¿no? R. Sí, sí. En mi cabeza está. Yo lo visualizo. P. Si, por lo que sea, no llega... R. Pues estaré satisfecha de haberlo intentado, de haber dado lo mejor de mí. Y bueno, es que tenemos muchas jugadoras muy buenas que están subiendo el nivel una barbaridad y cada vez es más difícil, así que vamos a pelear por ello. P. Te doy a elegir: ¿la final del Mundial o llegar a la final de Barcelona? R. ¡Qué buena pregunta! Yo creo que, si pudiese ser solo una de las dos, elegiría jugar el Mundial con España. P. ¿Qué tendría que pasar de aquí a diciembre para que dijeses: Mira, he tenido el año que quería tener? R. Al final, como son muchos días los que tiene el año, no es solo un resultado. Bueno, me encantaría llegar al final, como decimos, pero si tengo que decir algo un poco general, es eso: disfrutar cada día, ir con ganas a entrenar, que siga pasando eso que ha pasado tanto tiempo, que no desaparezca. P. Estás empezando prácticamente ahora proyecto con Aranza. ¿En qué momento se produce todo esto? ¿Cómo surge la unión? R. Pues ya veníamos con un proyecto con Alejandra Alonso en el que realmente no estábamos sabiendo sacar lo mejor la una de la otra, y la idea de cambiar fue un poco mutua también, para sacar ambas nuestra mejor versión. Y mira, lo de Aranza, en Valencia jugamos un partido de entrenamiento las dos después de haber sido eliminadas, con ella en el revés. Nos lo pasamos muy bien, luego nos fuimos a hacer un scape room, que nos gusta mucho a las dos, nos lo pasamos genial y luego, cuando decidimos acabar con Alejandra... pues se me quedó ahí. Pensé: ¿Con quién puedo jugar, que me apetezca, que rinda bien, que juegue bien y que ambas podamos rendir ya? Le llamé, me dijo que estaba dispuesta incluso a cambiarse de lado... y así surgió. Dijimos de ir poco a poco, viendo a lo mejor hasta el parón de verano. Luego hemos vuelto a hablar y hemos decidido seguir. O sea, que las dos estamos cómodas, a gusto, y eso es lo mejor para que el proyecto te divierta. P. ¿Qué te aporta Aranza? R. Me estaba faltando ese torbellino, esa alegría y contagio de que, a lo mejor, yo en momentos no estoy tan así como he sido siempre, por lo que sea, porque tienes días un poco más bajitos o con menos confianza... y tener al lado una persona como ella que es constante a más no poder, que es luchadora y que está plagada de energía, hace mucho. Está siempre dando buenas palabras y motivando, ojalá podamos seguir cosechando buenos resultados, pasándolo bien y rindiendo bien. P. ¿Crees honestamente, a día de hoy, que en el pádel estas cosas no se pueden decir, oye, 24 de agosto, pero crees que va a ser tu compañera, honestamente, de aquí al final de tu carrera? R. Sí, te diría que sí. Todo puede pasar y, evidentemente, sí. Si tiene una opción que le apetece, que es mejor, y le llega, pues tampoco estoy para cortar las alas a nadie. Y si ella lo decidiera así, pues así sería, ¿no? O sea, que yo creo que, por mi parte, estoy muy a gusto y perfectamente podemos terminar el año juntas. P. Ahora viene Madrid. Tú, Madrid... Te hago la pregunta más típica: ¿qué significa jugar para ti por última vez en Madrid, en tu sitio? R. Pues yo creo que va a ser una semana de las más especiales. Jugar en casa, con toda la gente, muchos recuerdos... Y, bueno, la verdad es que espero hacerlo bien, que no me puedan los nervios o la emoción porque tengo muchísimas ganas. Vengo de viajar un montón, esa especie de 'vaca-training', que ni son vacaciones ni es entrenamiento, pero venimos trabajando bien las últimas semanas y he podido seguir a tonto para llegar con pilas cargadas. El tramo final va a venir muy cargado de emociones para mí, va a ser más duro. P. ¿Va a venir mucha gente a verte a Madrid? Entiendo que familia, amigos... no se lo perderán. R. Me encanta que vengan a verme. Si bien no soy la jugadora, a lo mejor, que más mire fuera y, además, hoy en día, como muchas, lo que rodea la grada y todo, a veces es difícil focalizar en toda la gente que viene, pero sí que cuando tienes tu grupo más cercano, que está en el box, que está mucho más cerca de la pista, y les puedes ver, les puedes mirar cómo te apoyan con una mirada o con un gesto... Pues es muy bonito. P. Poder jugar en Madrid hace el cierre de su carrera, si cabe, un poco más perfecto, ¿no? R.
