A Barcelona me encanta. Es una ciudad en la que he estado mucho, que ha sido por momentos una segunda casa, también con varias compañeras con las que he ido mucho para allá. Soy fan de Barcelona, de la ciudad, y bueno, es otro sitio en el que he ganado mucho y del que tengo muy buenos recuerdos. Sería igualmente maravilloso si puedo llegar y despedirme allí. P. Y en noviembre, Mundial, que sería tu último. ¿Qué significaría para ti cerrar también esta etapa vistiendo los colores de la selección? R. Un sueño. Es quizá uno de los retos de este año. Aparte de focalizarme en el Tour Finals, también es jugar con la selección y poder ganar otro Mundial más con mi país y con mi gorro, que lleva 22 años conmigo y que está listo para un último viaje. P. ¿Te ves en la convocatoria? R. Ojalá tuviera la bola de cristal. Es que está igualado, pero puede que sí. P. Si te dijera: Dime la lista que harías tú... ¿Qué ocho jugadoras te llevarías tú al Mundial? R. Qué marrón... Me voy a ganar alguna enemiga, ya verás. A ver, vamos a ver. Gemma, Ari, Martina y Bea de reveses... y de derechas Paula, Andrea, Claudia... Y, si tuviera que pedir, pues sería yo la cuarta. P. Y con Carolina Navarro de seleccionadora. ¿Qué te pareció su elección? R. Me pareció fantástica, porque justo encima sucediendo a Iciar... ellas dos han sido mis maestras, mis dos referentes cuando era pequeña y de las que tuve luego la suerte de aprender a su lado en pista. Así que, vamos, cualquiera de las dos es más que válida, capaz y todos los adjetivos buenos que se te ocurran para este puesto. Carolina lo va a hacer muy bien porque ha seguido hasta casi hasta hace nada jugando, compitiendo, sabe todas las virtudes y las cosas a mejorar que tienen todas. Es una gran campeona y lo hará fenomenal. P. Hablabas hace poco en Bullpadel podcast junto a Nacho Palencia de la llamada de Gemma que no aceptaste para volver en 2023... ¿Qué se te pasaría por la cabeza pensando en un punto definitivo en la final y ganarlo junto a ella? R. ¿Dónde hay que firmar? Eso es lo que se me pasa por la cabeza. Sí, sería precioso jugar con ella. Además, lo hemos hablado hace poco. Podríamos haber jugado, no sé, alguna competición como la Hexagon Cup y haber tenido ese cierre diferente a lo que pasó. Y bueno... ¿por qué no en un Mundial? P. ¿Aquella llamada que no aceptaste es de estas cosas que, echando la vista atrás, piensas 'si pudiese viajar en el tiempo, lo cambiaría'? R. Quizás sí. Los deportistas estamos llenos de muchas cosas y de decisiones en cortos periodos de tiempo, con mucho cóctel alrededor, mucho en lo que pensar, y no siempre tomamos las mejores decisiones. Yo creo que a lo largo de mi carrera, en general, he tomado buenas y, a lo mejor, pues si volviera para atrás, esa sería una de las que a lo mejor me replantearía o la pensaría más. Tampoco tenía la bola de cristal y no sabía lo que iba a pasar después. Pero bueno, yo también tenía en ese momento un proyecto cerrado con Tamara. Luego Tamara se lesionó también bastantes meses... Entonces, claro, con el periódico del lunes, pues es más fácil decir: 'Bueno, sí, si al final hubiera vuelto a formar pareja con Gemma...'. Y quién sabe, a lo mejor hubiera salido mal. O no. Ha sido lo mismo, nadie lo sabe. Pero bueno, en general estoy satisfecha de las decisiones que he tomado, de lo que ha ido pasando a lo largo de mi carrera y, bueno, pues cuando se han venido mal dadas, de haber salido de ahí y haber vuelto a competir al nivel que yo quería. P. ¿Cuánto echas de menos ganar títulos? R. Muchísimo. Y la cosa es que no hace tanto. Yo me pongo a pensar y digo: 'Uy, hace tres años estaba levantando títulos'. P. ¿Cuándo fue tu último título? R. En el 2023, antes de operarme del codo, en Paraguay. P. Realmente, para una persona como tú que ha tenido la suerte de ganar muchísimo, tres años es un mundo. R. Claro. Es como que el cambio para mí ha sido más drástico... En el 2007 me puse top-3, y desde entonces hasta el 2023 son 17 años jugando prácticamente todos los sábados y casi todos los domingos. Ha sido una pasada. P. ¿Qué vas a hacer cuando dejes de jugar? Lo primero que vayas a hacer, aparte de irte de vacaciones, que es lo que se asume por las fechas en las que acaba la temporada. R. Dejar la pala por un tiempo. P. ¿Vas a ser capaz? R. Un poquito, unos días. No sé, no sé cuánto, pero unos días sí. P. ¿Has planeado ya algo para el tema del mantenimiento físico o vas a seguir? No sé si tienes un plan elaborado para seguir haciendo gimnasio, incluso, no sé, si haciendo pista. R. En mi cabeza tengo claro que voy a querer seguir con mis rutinas, manteniéndome activa tanto en el gimnasio como, por qué no, algún día en la pista. Todavía no he pensado eso, ni los horarios, ni cuántas horas, ni eso, pero ya habrá tiempo para pensar en eso. Y bueno, la idea es seguir manteniéndome activa. P. ¿Te da un poco de vértigo que llegue ese momento? R. No, tengo ganas. P. ¿Te apetece? R. Me apetece. Me apetece porque quiero hacer otras cosas. Tenemos ahora mucha ilusión con el proyecto de GOAT Sports Management, la agencia de representación, con eventos, cuidar a nuestros jugadores, con las marcas... Hace tres añitos que empezamos con ello y, bueno, la verdad es que está creciendo muchísimo y tengo ganas también de involucrarme mucho más. P. Hay momentos que en la vida de un deportista profesional, inevitablemente, te acabas perdiendo. ¿Apetece tener, digamos, menos ataduras para disfrutar con los tuyos? R. Por supuesto. Si hay algo que este año, además, con muchos de mis amigos y de gente cercana les digo es: 'Bueno, el año que viene voy a tener más tiempo'. Más tiempo para dedicárselo a ellos, para disfrutar sin prisas. Podré entrenar sin exigencias, ir al gimnasio y tomármelo mucho más pausado todo y no con esos objetivos tan exigentes y tan demandantes de la alta competición. Entonces, pues eso, sobre todo es como vivirlo todo un poco más pausado, tener más tiempo para todo y no ir a la carrera como vamos ahora. Hoy vengo corriendo, mañana tengo un avión, luego vuelvo a las 24 horas porque tengo otra cosa... Eso sí, quiero seguir trabajando ligada al pádel. Quiero seguir aportando mi granito de arena para que el deporte esté lo más alto posible, que sea olímpico en un futuro cercano. También ligada a las marcas que me han apoyado todo este tiempo y un montón de cosas que seguro que voy a hacer y que voy a tener la agenda ocupada, seguro, pero con más calma, con más tiempo para poder elegir también mi tiempo. P. ¿Dirías que es el gran peaje que paga un deportista profesional? El pasar menos tiempo con tu gente y perderte muchos momentos. R. Bueno, sí, me encantaría que pudiera ser, que la vida me dé un pequeñajo o una pequeñaja y darle todo mi cariño y mi amor para que sea una gran persona. P. Podría, puntualmente, a lo mejor el día de mañana, coachear algún equipo o algo puntual. En este caso, pues seleccionadora me haría mucha ilusión, pero en unos años. Claudia lo ha demostrado desde el día uno con ese súper reto con Gemma, que también es muy exigente, y Claudia ahí ya no es que diese la talla, es que creo que superó con creces lo que, a lo mejor, se podía esperar. Martina va también por ese camino y creo que son candidatas a ser números 1. Son muy buenas, están preparadas.. y lo que llegue pues llegará cuando toque. Me he sentido súper bien y, bueno, si bien de pequeña quizá era menos porque no había todo esto alrededor, poco a poco pues te vas haciendo a ello. Soy una persona a la que le gusta hablar, que le gusta debatir y, aunque pueda tener un poquito de nervios en según qué entrevista, en general no lo paso mal y me encanta conversar. Entonces creo que si algo te gusta, pues lo echarás de menos, estoy segura. Pero algo haremos... (sonríe).

articles.title: Erica Donald’s first reaction to husband Aaron Donald’s NFL return with the Rams is perfect
articles.summary: Aaron Donald has returned from retirement after three years away for the 2026 NFL season with the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams are making their push for a Supe...
articles.body:
Aaron Donald has returned from retirement after three years away for the 2026 NFL season with the Los Angeles Rams.

The Rams are making their push for a Super Bowl even stronger after successfully convincing Donald to return to the sport on a one-year, $20 million contract for another ring.

While the Rams will have Myles Garrett as their primary defensive star, Donald is a three-time DPOY who rejoins as a secondary defensive option behind the reigning DPOY. It's going to be a fun year for them.

Aaron Donald's wife reacts to the move on social media

After the news of Donald's return was confirmed, Erica Donald took to X and addressed the fans by joking about finally letting her husband back out of the house again.

It has to be a personal adjustment to see your husband go back to his incredibly physically demanding job for another season after spending a few seasons of retired life with them.

However, Donald has stayed in NFL-ready shape for a reason, and an opportunity like this is precisely what could entice him to return.

Erica and Aaron have been together since 2015, his second year in the NFL. The pair have a son together who was born in 2021, which influenced his decision to retire at the end of the 2023-24 season.

Now, he returns for what seems to be a one-year-only run to help the Rams win another Super Bowl after his role in the 2020-21 season.

Aaron Donald's return has a huge impact on the Rams

Donald has not played in two-and-a-half years, so there will be a considerable adjustment period over the first few weeks where the Rams use Donald as a rotational specialist instead of a full-time defensive starter.

Donald won't have to carry the individual defensive load he has had in past seasons with Garrett leading the line.

The team also added All-Pro C Trent McDuffie this offseason, showing how incredible the team can be defensively if all their stars stay healthy.

Teams will either be forced to double Donald or Garrett instead of being able to deploy two on either, which could be a nightmare for offensive OCs to figure out, provided Donald plays at the level we last saw him at.

Super Bowls are won on the field, so the Rams will hope their theoretical superteam can make it through the season healthy and remain effective come January.

articles.title: Djokovic falls in US Open first round, earliest Grand Slam exit in 20 years
articles.summary: Ailing Novak Djokovic suffered his earliest Grand Slam exit in 20 years on Sunday, falling in five brutal sets to Mariano Navone in the first round of the US...
articles.body:
Ailing Novak Djokovic suffered his earliest Grand Slam exit in 20 years on Sunday, falling in five brutal sets to Mariano Navone in the first round of the US Open.

The 48th-ranked Argentine's 7-6 (7/5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 victory ended Djokovic's latest bid for a record 25th Grand Slam title.

It also ended his run of 78 Grand Slam first-round victories, a streak stretching all the way back to Djokovic's 2006 loss to Paul Goldstein at the 2006 Australian Open.

Djokovic vomited on court and struggled with late-match cramps but appeared to have finally taken control when he broke Navone for a 2-1 lead in the fourth set with a vintage backhand winner down the line.

But Navone won the next five games, raising his arms in celebration after fighting off two break points for a 5-2 lead and breaking Djokovic again to force the fifth set.

Djokovic took a medical timeout before the final set, receiving massage on his spine and another delivery of medication.

But Navone jumped to a 3-0 lead in the decisive set and despite the urging of fans there was no road back for the Serb as his opponent dropped just one point on his own serve as he sprinted to the finish line.

"It's unbelievable," an ecstatic Navone said after triumphing in his first meeting with his longtime idol. "It's a dream come true, I mean seriously, 100%.

"This incredible court, the biggest stage ... Now I have to recover. I think it's almost 12 o'clock, so we have to go to sleep," he added after securing the win shortly before midnight after four hours and 36 minutes.

Djokovic broke Navone in the second game as he rolled to a 3-1 lead.

But the 39-year-old was clearly struggling and with Navone gaining confidence Djokovic had to claw out of 0-40 hole to hold for 4-1, looking weary as Navone began to extend the rallies.

Djokovic's double fault on break point allowed Navone to cut the deficit to 4-3, and after a brief pause to close the roof when showers struck Navone held at love to knot the set at 4-4.

Neither blinked until the tiebreaker, but pills delivered by the trainer didn't solve Djokovic's sluggishness.

He fell behind 4-2 in the tiebreaker and after a cleverly angled forehand winner to make it 5-5 Djokovic hit a forehand long and another into the net to give the set to Navone.

In a tense second set Djokovic missed break chances in the third and fifth games before breaking Navone at love for a 6-5 lead and holding at love to level the match at one set apiece.

The third set was more of the same, with Djokovic looking spent after every long rally.

He let a precious break chance go begging in the fifth game of the third and after Navone held for 3-2 Djokovic all but collapsed into his courtside chair and buried his face in a towel.

The Serb pressed on and was rewarded with a crucial break for a 5-4 lead. Navone made him work to serve out the set, saving a pair of set points and threatening to break before Djokovic held for a two sets to one lead.

He couldn't make the advantage stand. When it was all over, Djokovic embraced Navone, then departed blowing kisses to the crowd that had tried to will him to victory.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic loses in opening round of US Open for first time, falling in 5 sets to Mariano Navone
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic grinded through physical and internal ailments, made one mistake after another and could not find what it took to beat a feisty, younger oppon...
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic grinded through physical and internal ailments, made one mistake after another and could not find what it took to beat a feisty, younger opponent who was not intimidated under the lights against tennis' most decorated player.

The 39-year-old is out of the US Open after a first-round defeat to Mariano Navone on Sunday night, losing 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 in a five-set marathon that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. It was the longest opening match of a Grand Slam in Djokovic's career and became his earliest exit in two decades, dating to the 2006 Australian Open. He had never lost in the first round at the US Open.

"I didn't enjoy myself," Djokovic said. "I think it was obvious that it was an awful feeling on the court for me."

The record holder with 24 major titles threw up at least once and later appeared to be cramping when he grabbed at his left foot. Djokovic swallowed pills brought to him by a doctor and had his lower back massaged during a medical timeout between the fourth and fifth sets, and he grimaced after several shots.

Djokovic made 70 unforced errors in a painful performance that ended mere minutes before midnight.

"It's something that I've been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year: vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there," Djokovic said. "Then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain. Yeah, the back just gave up in the end and shoulder, and I couldn't close it out."

With this defeat, 21 years to the day of his US Open debut, the question now lingers as to whether this was Djokovic's final match at this or any Grand Slam. After the loss, he said he was "trying to address really what's going on and how far I can go this way."

It was clear Djokovic was not himself, and the wear and tear of sickness and soreness took its toll. The No. 4 seed from Serbia cruised to early 3-0 and 4-1 leads before blowing them and losing the first set — the first time that happened to him in the first round of the US Open since '06.

"Just struggled all the way since the fourth game of the match," Djokovic said. "When it comes to match itself and overall feeling of how I felt with body and playing, it was really not enjoyable. I pretty much despised every moment that I spent on the court for that.

With his wife, Jelena, watching from the stands with worried looks on her face, Djokovic had moments where he looked like one of the best to play the sport. His fist pump was reserved after winning the second set, and he put his hand to his ear and gestured to the crowd for applause on the way to taking the third.

But Navone — a 25-year-old from Argentina who earlier this year won his first ATP singles title — did not go away.

Neither did the frustration of not being healthy or at his best. After firing a shot wide in the fourth set, Djokovic landed awkwardly and dropped his racket.

Djokovic all but conceded the fourth set. But he was unable to muster enough for the what would have been his 43rd five-set victory as Navone picked up his first, calling it a dream come true.

"(It) was very tough for me because you are playing with the 'GOAT' on this court," said Navone, who idolized Djokovic growing up. "For sure it's the best thing I've had on court. This is an amazing court and the biggest stage. It's amazing, the way we play. I mean, five sets. … I'm very happy. I don't know. What can I say?"

It extended a nightmare stretch for Djokovic, who also lost in the first round at the hardcourt tuneup in Cincinnati earlier this month. That was his first action since losing to top-ranked Jannik Sinner in the semifinals at Wimbledon.

Djokovic expressed hope Saturday that his early exit at Cincinnati gave him more time to prepare for the US Open but acknowledged concern that the first match at any tournament has become challenging for him in recent years. Instead of overcoming the hurdle and building from there, he is left to contemplate an uncertain future.

His fist pump was reserved after winning the second set, and he put his hand to his ear and gestured to the crowd for applause on the way to taking the third.

But Navone — a 25-year-old from Argentina who earlier this year won his first ATP singles title — did not go away.

Neither did the frustration of not being healthy or at his best. After firing a shot wide in the fourth set, Djokovic landed awkwardly and dropped his racket.

Djokovic all but conceded the fourth set. But he was unable to muster enough for the what would have been his 43rd five-set victory as Navone picked up his first, calling it a dream come true.

"(It) was very tough for me because you are playing with the 'GOAT' on this court," said Navone, who idolized Djokovic growing up. "For sure it's the best thing I've had on court. This is an amazing court and the biggest stage. It's amazing, the way we play. I mean, five sets. … I'm very happy. I don't know. What can I say?"

It extended a nightmare stretch for Djokovic, who also lost in the first round at the hardcourt tuneup in Cincinnati earlier this month. That was his first action since losing to top-ranked Jannik Sinner in the semifinals at Wimbledon.

Djokovic expressed hope Saturday that his early exit at Cincinnati gave him more time to prepare for the US Open but acknowledged concern that the first match at any tournament has become challenging for him in recent years. Instead of overcoming the hurdle and building from there, he is left to contemplate an uncertain future.

articles.title: Will Stanford Women's Basketball's Non-Conference Schedule Snap Tournament Drought?
articles.summary: Stanford's non-conference slate has plenty of challenges throughout the schedule, but those first two months also present an opportunity to build up some lee...
articles.body:
Regardless of which programs are on the schedule in 2026-27, the goal for Stanford women's basketball has to be to rack up enough wins to break a two-year drought of missing the NCAA tournament.

Those two seasons have come under head coach Kate Paye, who took over in 2024-25, following the retirement of Tara VanDerveer. Every season since 1987-88 that there was a tournament, VanDerveer led the program to the tournament, so there is a standard of excellence for the Cardinal on the court.

The other big change that occurred in this same time period is that Stanford moved from the Pac-12 to the ACC, finishing with an 8-10 conference record in each of the past two seasons. That is the same conference record the Cardinal held in 1986-87, the season before their streak began.

Improving the ACC record will be one key way for Stanford to play meaningful games in March. Another will be to dominate the non-conference schedule, which the program announced recently.

On Saturday, October 24 and Wednesday, October 28, Stanford will host exhibition matchups against Pacific (10/24) and UC Santa Barbara (10/28).

Monday, November 2 — Arizona (TNT Sports Hall of Fame Series Las Vegas)

Wednesday, November 4 — Saint Mary's (Home)

Friday, November 13 — Santa Clara (Away)

Friday, November 27 — Columbia (Honolulu, HI)

Saturday, November 28 — San Diego State (Honolulu, HI)

Sunday, November 29 — Hawai'i (Honolulu, HI)

Wednesday, December 2 — Auburn ( ACC/SEC Challenge in Auburn, AL)

Thursday, December 17 — Arizona State (Home)

Sunday, December 20 — Ohio State (Invisalign Bay Area Women's Classic in SF)

Stanford will have a month-long gap in between home games from November 15 against Gonzaga to December 17 against ASU. The break from December 2nd through the 17th is customary each season to account for final exams.

Conference home games (dates to be announced): Boston College, California, Florida State, Georgia Tech, Miami, NC State, North Carolina, Pittsburgh and Syracuse. That's nine home conference games.

Conference road games (dates to be announced): Cal, Clemson, Duke, Louisville, Notre Dame, SMU, Virginia, Virginia Tech and Wake Forest. That is another nine road conference games.

The non-conference schedule contains five games at neutral locations, five games at home, and another four on the road. Last year they finished with a 21-14 record overall. This year, the non-conference schedule will be about finding some cohesion with all of the roster moves the program made .

With only 12 players on the roster, that initial two months will be about chasing wins, but also building up that depth and keeping the key cogs of the team fresh for those ACC games.

articles.title: 32 Days to Opening Night: Claude Lemieux
articles.summary: Over the years, a number of players have worn the number 32 for the San Jose Sharks. This summer though, it seems like a disservice to his legendary career t...
articles.body:
Over the years, a number of players have worn the number 32 for the San Jose Sharks. This summer though, it seems like a disservice to his legendary career to discuss any player other than the late Claude Lemieux, who tragically passed away in May.

Lemieux was drafted in the 1983 NHL Draft with the 26th overall pick by the Montreal Canadiens. A native of Buckingham, Quebec, Lemieux had to move just two hours away from his hometown to join his new team. He made his NHL debut during the 1984-85 season, appearing in just a single game that year. The following season, he got another short stint in the NHL as he appeared in 10 games but earned his first Stanley Cup at the end of the postseason.

Lemieux truly established himself as an NHL regular during the 1986-87 season, playing in 76 games. That season, he scored 27 goals and had 56 points, but also notably registered 156 penalty minutes as well.

At the end of the decade, Lemieux was traded to the New Jersey Devils after six seasons with the Canadiens. Lemieux spent five seasons with the Devils, winning his second Stanley Cup and his only Conn Smythe Trophy during the 1994-95 season.

Following the Stanley Cup victory, Lemieux was on the move again, this time to Colorado. He joined the Avalanche right after they relocated from Quebec City and lifted the Stanley Cup for the third time in his first season in Denver. After five partial seasons with Colorado, he returned to New Jersey for the second half of the 1999-00 season and won his fourth Stanley Cup.

After his final Stanley Cup, Lemieux spent some time with the Phoenix Coyotes and had a short stint with the Dallas Stars. He then retired from the NHL following the 2002-03 season, notably without playing for the Sharks. So, dear reader, if you're a newer fan, you may be asking how he relates to the Sharks.

After a considerable amount of time away from the NHL, Lemieux made a shocking return to join the Sharks during the 2008-09 season. He only played 18 games at the NHL level, spending the most of his time in the organization in the AHL, but he officially ended his NHL career in San Jose.

Lemieux is remembered as one of the NHL's best agitators, as he loved to get under the skin of his opponents, but he also wasn't afraid to stand up for himself or a teammate, although it was usually the result of his own antics.

articles.title: Why Avalanche making Cale Makar highest-paid NHL player ever was a no-brainer
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche made history recently with their new contract for Cale Makar. The Avalanche defenseman is set to earn $20.4 million per season, makin...
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche made history recently with their new contract for Cale Makar. The Avalanche defenseman is set to earn $20.4 million per season, making him the highest-paid player in league history . His $163.2 million total contract value is also the highest handed out to any player.

This is a monumental contract for a few reasons. Makar is not making the max salary that a player can make under the current cap environment. The max contract is $20.8 million per season, which works out to a total value of $166.4 under an eight-year term. But he is the first player to command anywhere near that amount on a contract extension.

This is a new age for the National Hockey League. This is a sport that is only just getting used to players making $10 million in a single season. The league has worked hard to wiggle out of the flat cap era since the beginning of the 2020s. Now, general managers have cash to spend. Evidently, they are not afraid to do so.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Of course, when contracts this size come down the pike, they draw a ton of attention. Add in Makar's status as one of the best defensemen in the NHL , and this deal had the hockey world abuzz. Many chimed in with their opinions and hot takes after news of this signing was confirmed.

Some criticized the amount of money the star defenseman received. However, the Avalanche made the right decision by paying up for Makar. For this franchise, it was an easy choice to make. In some ways, it was also the only choice to make.

The Avalanche could not afford to lose Cale Makar at any cost

In a team-oriented sport such as hockey, placing too much value on one single player can be dangerous. However, there are always exceptions to the rule. Cale Makar is one of those exceptions.

Admittedly, Makar's defensive game does leave a little to be desired. Since the 2019-20 season, for example, the Avalanche star has the highest Goals Against Expected per 82 games in the NHL, according to HockeyStats.com. He isn't a major liability, but his defensive game is not his strong suit.

Offensively, though, there are few defensemen like him in the league. He leads all defenders with at least 100 games played since 2019-20 in Goals Per 82 games and Points per 82 games. Few defensemen in the NHL can rival him offensively.

This is one of the main reasons the Avalanche needed to pay the big bucks. Colorado knows the value Makar brings is rivaled by only a few players. More importantly, there is no chance the Avalanche have what it would take to replace their franchise defenseman if he left in NHL Free Agency next summer.

Players who fit the offensive mold, such as Evan Bouchard or Zach Werenski, are unattainable. Potential trade targets like Adam Fox would be well out of the price range for the Avalanche. More defensive options, such as Moritz Seider, are also simply unattainable.

The Avalanche could have made a play for Quinn Hughes in NHL Free Agency next summer. But if they were to do that, they would likely need to pay the max for a shorter-term contract. The NHL is lowering contract term limits from eight years on a contract extension to seven years in the next Collective Bargaining Agreement. Free-agent contracts would be capped at six years.

This isn't to mention the cost, either. The maximum contract rate will increase in 2027. This means that the Avalanche would need to pay more for Hughes and have less team control in the process.

Colorado knows what it has in Makar, and it knows the value he brings isn't easily matched by other players. The Avalanche needed to keep their franchise defenseman around, as they had no chance of replacing him. If that meant making him the highest-paid player in NHL history, then that's the cost of business.

articles.title: Chiefs Cut Ties With 5-Year Quarterback as Justin Fields Decision Looms
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have cut ties with a veteran quarterback amid a plethora of roster moves. The post Chiefs Cut Ties With 5-Year Quarterback as Justin F...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs finalized the team's 53-man roster which led to some challenging decisions. Kansas City announced a plethora of roster cuts, including one veteran quarterback, amid the NFL's roster deadline on Sunday, August 30.

The Chiefs have their franchise quarterback in Patrick Mahomes. Behind the star, a battle has been brewing between Justin Fields and Garrett Nussmeier for the backup quarterback role.

Kansas City also had a fourth quarterback on the roster until the team finalized the team's 53 players. The Chiefs announced that veteran quarterback Chris Oladokun has been released with an injury designation.

Oladokun had been in concussion protocol during the preseason. It remains to be seen if the Chiefs will look to re-sign Oladokun to the team's practice squad.

Kansas City may pass on bringing back Oladokun given the Chiefs opted to keep both Fields and Nussmeier on the roster. With Mahomes appearing to be healthy, there does not appear to be a pressing need to have four quarterbacks.

Here's what you need to know about the latest Chiefs news amid a series of roster cuts.

Who Will Chiefs Name as QB2: Justin Fields or Garrett Nussmeier?

Nussmeier has had a strong preseason, but it would still be a surprise if the rookie is able to unseat Fields as the Chiefs QB2. The Chiefs traded for Fields this offseason as insurance behind Mahomes who was just a few months removed from sustaining a season-ending ACL injury at the time.

Now that the roster is finalized, Kansas City will eventually need to name a backup quarterback. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid still sounds impressed with Fields.

"Yeah, I like him," Reid said of Fields during the preseason. "He's a good kid.

"He works his tail (off), very smart, and has done some nice things there. You'd have to ask him that question (how Fields is adapting to Chiefs system). But I like what I've seen, yeah. He's done a nice job."

articles.summary: Former Buffalo Bills wide receiver Isaiah Hodgins was cut by the New York Giants at the final roster deadline. The post Former Bills Draft Pick WR Cut Loose...
articles.body:
A former Buffalo Bills player has hit the open market three years after he was poached by the New York Giants.

The Giants announced on Sunday that they parted ways with veteran receiver Isaiah Hodgins, who was a regular part of their offense since joining the team in 2023. Hodgins will now become a free agent, with a potential return to New York in the cards.

The Giants released Hodgins as part of their final roster cuts, with NFL teams required to whittle their 90-man summer rosters down to 53 players by Sunday at 6 p.m.

The Bills initially drafted Hodgins with a sixth-round pick in 2020, but he missed his rookie season after being placed on injured reserve. He was assigned to Buffalo's practice squad the next season, appearing in just one game that year. The Bills waived Hodgins again in 2022 after he was elevated to the practice squad, but the Giants picked him up off waivers.

Hodgins appeared in 35 games for the Giants across four seasons with 14 starts. He made 66 receptions for 708 yards with eight touchdowns for the Giants.

Hodgins was one of several former Bills players to suit up for the Giants, who hired former Bills offensive coordinator Brian Daboll as their head coach and former Bills assistant general manager Joe Schoen as their GM.

articles.title: Mariners calling up slugging OF prospect Lazaro Montes per several reports
articles.summary: It’s time for big swings in Seattle.
articles.body:
Longtime baseball reporter Francys Romero reported Sunday evening that Cuban OF Lazaro Montes will be called up to the Seattle Mariners, with Daniel Kramer of MLB.com reporting that the move is expected ahead of Tuesday's game in Boston, coinciding with the expansion of rosters to 28 for September call-ups. Montes is in transit to Boston but is not necessarily expected to be activated for Monday's series opener at the Red Sox.

Montes has been one of the most powerful sluggers in the minor leagues since arriving in pro ball after training in the Dominican Republic as a teenager. Progressing through the same program that produced Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez, the comparisons for the titanic lefty have been common. They're not quite accurate, however. Montes is a huge kid, a 21 year old listed at 6'5, 210 whose frame is as massive as his smile. Like Alvarez, while he moves well for his size, his gait and foot speed are never going to reflect as plus defensively, though Montes has good baseline athleticism that helps him make many 50/50 plays despite middling range. Moreover, his arm is absolutely massive, a profile similar to an early-career Nelson Cruz. Not just that, but Montes is a high-effort player in all phases, occasionally stunning opponents with his pace and hustle.

But that's not the main thing Lazaro Montes is all about. The reason he's been a top-100 prospect and one of the most anticipated hitting prospects in years for Seattle is gargantuan power that's seen him club 21 homers in 2024 across 542 PA at a teenager, then 32 a season ago between High-A and Double-A, and now 38 big flies in 537 PA across Arkansas and Triple-A Tacoma. At every level, Montes has been a variation of highly consistent, slugging massively, walking prominently, and whiffing most of the time he's not doing one of those two options.

It's made for a fascinating profile, with a .247/.365/.556 line this season that features a 14.3% walk rate and a 30.7% strikeout rate. The in-zone contact rate on Montes' swings (and contact rate overall) is poor enough that there are plenty of folks who simply don't think he can be a big leaguer in an effective long-term capacity, despite doing devastating damage most of the time he makes contact. Montes has a 71.1% in-zone contact rate and 64.4% contact overall on swings in his ~200 plate appearances with the Rainiers, where Statcast data is tracked throughout the Pacific Coast League publicly. The only qualified hitter worse than that at the big league level is 1B Munetaka Murakami of the Chicago White Sox, who is at 70.5% and 60.7% respectively. Nobody else is below 77% for in-zone contact, and even if you drop the big league split to minimum of 200 PAs, it's only Murakami lower.

The key for Montes is what he does on contact. His hard hit rate in Tacoma is 56.8% per Statcast, which is again a number in company with only Murakami, James Wood, Oneil Cruz, Nick Kurtz, Pete Alonso, and Aaron Judge. His hardest hit ball in Triple-A this year is 116.3 MPH, which ties Wood, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Elly De La Cruz for 8th-hardest in MLB all year. His average exit velocity would be third-highest in MLB behind just Cruz and Wood, right ahead of Yordan. The more likely outcome than instant stardom is something closer to what we've seen from Jordan Walker, Coby Mayo, or Jac Caglianone, all of whom share similar offensive profiles, explosive strength, and risk of whiff in their swing.

The choice of Montes makes sense in terms of production, he's crushed every level at every age he's been assigned. His profile, however, is an intriguing one to see, and may be indicative of Seattle's willingness to hope for a hail mary, looking to Lazaro to bring their season back from the dead with a deluge of big flies. Being called up in September will not impact Montes' ability to be a rookie in 2027, nor disrupt his eligibility for the Prospect Promotion Incentive picks the have ample value to clubs. Whether Montes posts daily or in a part-time role may depend on what the M's are valuing in their final month of play.

(Photo by Caton Marsh/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images)

articles.title: Alabama Has the Best Quarterback Duo in College Football With Keelon Russell and Austin Mack
articles.summary: Kalen DeBoer secures a dominant future in Tuscaloosa, pairing five-star phenomenon Keelon Russell with veteran depth to create the nation's most formidable a...
articles.body:
There are quarterback rooms across college football with more experience. There are quarterbacks who have already put up bigger numbers. There are returning starters with Heisman Trophy hype and NFL Draft buzz. But if you ask me which team has the best combination of a starting quarterback and backup quarterback heading into the 2026 season, I am taking Alabama.

And I really do not think people understand yet just how fortunate Alabam a is to have both of them.

Russell has officially won the starting quarterback job, and I have made it pretty clear how excited I am about that decision. I believe Kalen DeBoer made the right call. Russell has an incredibly high ceiling, tremendous natural ability and the potential to become one of the biggest stars in college football.

But here is what makes Alabama's quarterback situation different:

If something happens to Russell, Alabama does not suddenly have a quarterback problem.

They have Austin Mack. That is why I believe Alabama may have the best QB duo in America. Not necessarily because Russell and Mack are going to finish first and second in the Heisman Trophy voting.

That is not what I am saying. I am talking about the combination.

Talent, depth, experience, upside and the ability to win football games regardless of which one is standing behind center. There may not be another team in America that can feel as comfortable about its first two quarterbacks as Alabama should right now.

Russell is the exciting young superstar. Mack is the experienced, talented backup who could start for plenty of programs around college football.

Russell arrived at Alabama as one of the highest-rated quarterback recruits in the country. The former five-star prospect was rated among the very best players in the entire 2025 recruiting class after an incredible high school career at Duncanville. During his final high school season, Russell threw for 3,652 yards, 52 touchdowns and only two interceptions while completing more than 71 percent of his passes. He was also named the Gatorade National Player of the Year.

But Russell has never just been about numbers.

The arm talent is there. The athleticism is there. The confidence is there.

He can extend plays with his legs. He can make throws from different platforms. He can attack defenses vertically. And most importantly, he seems to have that natural quarterback instinct that is very difficult to teach. Last season, Russell only appeared in two games for Alabama, but he completed 11 of 15 passes for 143 yards and two touchdowns.

Obviously, that is an incredibly small sample size. But this summer and fall were about something completely different.

Russell had to prove he could actually command Alabama's offense. He had to prove he could handle protections. He had to prove he could make adjustments before the snap. He had to prove he could operate Ryan Grubb's offense when the defense showed him something unexpected. And according to Alabama's coaches, he did exactly that.

This was not some quarterback competition where Russell was handed the position because he was a former five-star recruit.

Austin Mack made him earn it. That is another reason I am so excited about Russell. He had to beat a really good quarterback.

Mack knows DeBoer's system better than almost anybody in Alabama's quarterback room.

He originally played for DeBoer at Washington before following him to Tuscaloosa. He has spent multiple years developing inside this offensive system, learning the terminology, protections, reads and expectations that come with playing quarterback for DeBoer.

Last season, Mack served as the primary backup behind Ty Simpson and completed 24 of 32 passes for 228 yards and two touchdowns. He also got meaningful playing time against Indiana in the College Football Playoff, completing 11 of 16 passes for 103 yards.

Across his Alabama appearances over the last two seasons, Mack has completed 26 of 35 passes for 267 yards and three touchdowns.

Again, those are not Heisman numbers. Nobody is pretending they are. But they show something important. Mack is not some random backup quarterback Alabama hopes can survive if something happens to Russell.

He can play. And Alabama's coaches know it.

Throughout the quarterback competition, DeBoer and his staff repeatedly talked about how comfortable they were with both players.

At one point, DeBoer essentially said Alabama felt like it could go into the season with either quarterback. Even after Russell officially won the job, offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb emphasized that the coaching staff had confidence it could win at a high level with either one.

Because there is a difference between having a backup quarterback and having another starting-caliber quarterback sitting behind your starter.

That is where this quarterback room becomes so dangerous. Russell brings the ceiling. Mack brings security. Russell gives Alabama that dynamic playmaking ability that can completely change an offense. Mack gives Alabama a veteran option who understands what DeBoer and Grubb want to accomplish.

Both understand the offense. Both were good enough to make this quarterback competition last deep into August. That should tell Alabama fans something.

If Mack were not a good quarterback, Russell would have been named the starter months ago. Instead, Alabama's coaching staff had a legitimate decision to make. Russell ultimately won it. But Mack did not suddenly become less talented because someone else won the competition.

Actually, DeBoer has been very intentional about making that point.

After naming Russell the starter, DeBoer made it clear that Mack had not failed and had not suddenly lost standing in the program simply because Russell earned QB1. He praised Mack's work ethic, professionalism and willingness to continue supporting the team.

That might be my favorite part of this entire quarterback situation. Because talent matters. But chemistry matters too.

There are quarterback rooms where a competition ends and things become awkward. The backup is mad. The starter knows the backup is mad. Players start choosing sides. Every interception becomes a quarterback controversy. Every bad quarter turns into people screaming for the backup. That can become toxic very quickly.

But everything we have heard suggests Russell and Mack genuinely have a good relationship.

Mack has supported Russell. Russell has earned Mack's respect. And Alabama has two quarterbacks who competed against each other without allowing that competition to become bigger than the team.

That is enormous. Especially when you consider how young Russell still is.

He is going to make mistakes. Let me say that again because Alabama fans need to understand it before the season even begins. Keelon Russell is going to make mistakes. He is a young quarterback.

There will probably be an interception at some point that makes you want to throw the remote. There may be a missed read. There may be a bad quarter. There may even be a bad game.

That does not mean Alabama should immediately panic. It also does not mean Mack should immediately replace him.

Russell needs room to develop. But having Mack behind him gives Alabama something incredibly valuable while that development happens.

If Russell gets hurt, Alabama has another quarterback who can run the offense. If Russell's helmet comes off for a play, Mack can walk onto the field. If Alabama needs Mack for a series, a quarter, a game or longer, he can step in. And Alabama does not have to completely throw out its offense.

That is such a luxury in college football. We have seen championship dreams disappear because a starting quarterback got hurt. We have seen teams with loaded rosters become completely different because the backup could not operate the offense. Alabama should not have that problem.

And Alabama fans know better than almost anyone why backup quarterbacks matter.

We watched Tua Tagovailoa come off the bench in the national championship game against Georgia. We watched Jalen Hurts come off the bench the next season in the SEC Championship Game and save Alabama against Georgia. Two of the biggest moments in modern Alabama football history involved the backup quarterback being ready.

That lesson should never be forgotten in Tuscaloosa.

Sometimes QB2 becomes the guy who saves your season.

That does not mean Mack is going to have some dramatic Jalen Hurts moment this season. Maybe Russell starts every game and Mack only appears in blowouts. Alabama would probably be thrilled if that happens because it would likely mean Russell stayed healthy and played great football. But championships are built partly on preparing for situations you hope never happen. That is why Mack is so valuable.

He gives Alabama an answer to a question other teams desperately hope they never have to ask: What happens if our starting quarterback cannot play?

For Alabama? You send in Austin Mack. That is a pretty darn good answer. And there is another reason I would put this duo against anybody in America.

They make each other better. Russell had to beat Mack. Mack had to compete against Russell. Neither quarterback had the luxury of coasting through the offseason knowing the job belonged to him.

Every practice mattered. Every meeting mattered. Every scrimmage mattered. Every throw mattered.

That competition should make Alabama better. Russell knows there is a talented quarterback behind him. Mack knows he must remain ready because his opportunity could come at any moment.

And Alabama may benefit from that all season.

There is so much attention placed on who starts at quarterback that sometimes we forget football seasons are long. Especially now.

If Alabama wants to win the SEC Championship and make another run through the College Football Playoff, this could become a 15- or 16-game season. That is a lot of football. Bodies get beat up. Players get injured. Unexpected things happen. Depth becomes incredibly important. And at the most important position on the field, Alabama has it.

That should terrify opposing teams. Because Russell's ceiling is massive. I believe he has the talent to become one of the best quarterbacks in college football.

Maybe not eventually. Maybe this year. There are going to be growing pains because that comes with being a young quarterback, but there is something different about his talent. And if Russell becomes what Alabama believes he can become, this offense could be special.

Then you remember Alabama has Mack standing beside him. A 6-foot-6 quarterback who already understands the system, has played college football and very nearly won the starting job himself. That is why I keep coming back to the same conclusion.

Give me Alabama's quarterback duo against anybody. There may be teams with a more established QB1. There may be teams with a quarterback who has thrown for 3,000 yards. There may be individual quarterbacks ranked ahead of Russell entering the season simply because they have done more at the college level.

But when we are talking about the entire top of the quarterback depth chart? QB1 plus QB2? I am taking Keelon Russell and Austin Mack.

Russell gives Alabama championship-level upside. Mack gives Alabama championship-level depth.

Russell gives you electricity. Mack gives you experience.

Russell is Alabama's starter. Mack is probably good enough to start at a lot of places.

And somehow Alabama gets to have both. That is what makes this quarterback room special.

The Crimson Tide does not just have a quarterback it believes can win. It has two. Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb spent the entire offseason saying essentially that.

Russell earned QB1. Mack handled QB2 like a professional. And now Alabama enters the 2026 season knowing that whichever quarterback has to take a meaningful snap, the coaching staff believes in him.

Keelon Russell may be the face of Alabama's offense this season. Austin Mack may be standing on the sideline waiting for his opportunity. But do not confuse different roles with different importance. Alabama needs them both. And by the time this season is over, college football may realize what Alabama already knows.

The Crimson Tide does not just have one really good quarterback.

And that might give Alabama the best quarterback duo in America.

articles.title: NASCAR’s Chase Is Back: Here’s How the 2026 Format Works
articles.summary: NASCAR’s championship format changed for 2026, so before the final 10 races begin, let’s make The Chase make sense. Following the 26-race regular season, the...
articles.body:
NASCAR's championship format changed for 2026, so before the final 10 races begin, let's make The Chase make sense.

Following the 26-race regular season, the top 16 drivers in the Cup Series standings advance to The Chase. Unlike the previous playoff format, winning a race does not automatically secure a spot. Drivers must earn their way into the championship battle through points.

Once the field is set, the standings reset based on each driver's regular-season position. The regular-season champion begins The Chase with 2,100 points, followed by the second seed at 2,075 and the third at 2,065. From there, the total decreases by five points per position until the 16th seed starts at 2,000.

That creates a 100-point gap between first and 16th before the postseason even begins, rewarding drivers for an entire season of consistency rather than treating every qualifier equally.

Then, it becomes a 10-race sprint to the championship.

There are no elimination rounds, cutoff races or Championship 4. All 16 contenders remain eligible throughout The Chase, and the driver with the most points following the finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway becomes the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series champion.

Winning still matters, though. Race winners now receive 55 points, 15 more than under the previous system, while a perfect race featuring two stage wins and the overall victory is worth 75 points. That means one dominant afternoon can create a significant swing in the standings, but a single win alone cannot advance or eliminate anyone.

The Chase name originally debuted in 2004, but NASCAR's 2026 version combines that familiar 10-race championship run with a renewed emphasis on season-long performance. The simplest way to follow it? No brackets and no automatic advancement, just 16 drivers accumulating points across 10 races, with every position carrying championship consequences.

articles.title: Heat Could Change Their Head Coach After Erik Spoelstra Will Complete 20 Years In 2028
articles.summary: After completing 20 years as the Heat head coach, Erik Spoelstra could be due for a big change.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat are known as a storied franchise in the NBA. Under Pat Riley 's influence in the '90s, the "Heat Culture" became the team's foundation and philosophy. Although Riley transitioned to a front-office role later in his career, Miami's philosophy remained as Erik Spoelstra took over as head coach in 2008.

Although the Miami Heat were competitive under Pat Riley, the Heat became a different monster under Erik Spoelstra. From managing superstars like Dwyane Wade and LeBron James to nurturing the newer generation of stars like Bam Adebayo , Spoelstra has been one of the most impactful coaches in NBA history .

Currently, Erik Spoelstra also serves as head coach for the USA men's national team ahead of the 2028 Olympics, which will mark the end of his three-year cycle in the role. Coincidentally, 2028 will also mark 20 years since Spoelstra took over the Heat head coaching role, and according to Heat insider Ira Winderman, it may be the ideal opportunity for him to make a move. Winderman shared :

"When you talk about the Heat turnaround, after the 2028 Los Angeles games, to me, it would be the natural time for Spo to maybe move to the front office to step back."

"Right now, I know he loves it. It would make sense. But who knows? Maybe he's one of those coaching lifers. Maybe he's Hubie, and he's going to come back, you know, in a different way and keep doing that, just like I think Pat Riley will never fade away."

Spoelstra is the longest-tenured coach not only in the NBA, but in all four major sports across the USA. Given that his career with the Heat began as a video coordinator in 1995, Erik Spoelstra's loyalty and commitment to the franchise are beyond question.

Does this mean he should continue as head coach, though?

It is quite common for coaches to eventually transition from their roles and join the front office, primarily functioning as executives. Pat Riley is a prime example, as he went from being a coach to serving as president of the Miami Heat.

Although Riley made this move much later in his career, Brad Stevens is another prominent example of a young coach who opted for a front office role. Considering that Stevens embraced a role as the Boston Celtics ' president (replacing Danny Ainge ) after serving only eight years as head coach, it is clear that there is no strict format or pipeline for such moves.

In many ways, should Spoelstra opt to move into a front office role, his transition would look like a blend of Brad Stevens and Spurs president Gregg Popovich . While this could be largely positive, the circumstances may not necessarily support Spoelstra's departure.

This offseason has been particularly eventful for the Miami Heat, as it finally saw the franchise acquire another bona fide superstar in Giannis Antetokounmpo . With a new star duo leading the franchise, Spoelstra's influence will prove vital in keeping the Heat competitive this season. But how long could this core sustain without him?

Giannis Antetokounmpo currently has the luxury of exercising a $62.7 million player option next summer. While this would ideally see him remain with Miami through the 2027-28 season, Spoelstra's potential departure at the end of the 2028 offseason could drastically affect Antetokounmpo's decision in free agency.

The Heat's current situation is still quite promising, as it allows them to convince Antetokounmpo to stay with the promise of being competitive. However, if Spoelstra's influence as head coach is deemed a vital factor, Miami may not wish to see the 55-year-old leave his current position unless they find a suitable replacement. Needless to say, that pursuit could also prove challenging.

articles.title: How Aston Villa could line-up against Arsenal after woeful start to the Premier League season
articles.summary: Aston Villa could hardly have imagined a worse start to the 2026/27 Premier League season.The Lions were torn apart by Brighton & Hove Albion at the Amex Sta...
articles.body:
Aston Villa could hardly have imagined a worse start to the 2026/27 Premier League season.

The Lions were torn apart by Brighton & Hove Albion at the Amex Stadium, with Fabian Hurzeler's side needing just 31 minutes to put the game beyond doubt.

A Victor Lindelof own goal and a debut red card for Joao Gomes summed up a disastrous afternoon for Villa, who were forced into the relegation zone after losing 4-0 on opening day.

It's too early to say whether the heavy defeat points to deeper problems following the departures of several high-profile players including Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa, and Lucas Digne.

However, the Villans have sprung into action in the transfer market.

Leon Goretzka has arrived to add experience and quality to midfield, while Nicolas Jackson will take over as Ollie Watkins' successor in attack .

Both players will be keen to help Villa recover from their opening-day thrashing, but their next challenge doesn't get any bigger as they host Arsenal.

Fortunately for the Lions, they have a decent record against the Premier League champions at Villa Park.

Villa have won their last three home league games against champions, beating Liverpool last season after previous victories over Manchester City in the 2023/24 and 2024/25.

Villa supporters will also remember Emiliano Buendia's dramatic late winner against Arsenal last season.

That result was Villa's fourth victory in seven home league meetings with the Gunners, although Arsenal responded with a 4-1 thrashing in the reverse fixture.

After kicking off the campaign with a 4-0 thrashing at the hands of Brighton, Villa have moved quickly to bolster key areas of their decimated squad.

One of the new faces is goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who was brought in to replace the experienced Emiliano Martinez. The Japanese goalie could be handed his debut against Arsenal later today.

He'll have a much-changed Villa backline ahead of him with Matteo Ruggeri and Matty Cash lining up on either side of Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof.

Lamare Bogarde and Boubacar Kamara should anchor the midfield while Ross Barkley joins Emiliano Buendia and John McGinn in providing support for new striker Nicolas Jackson.

The Senegalese striker completed a sensational reunion with Emery in the past few days and will be keen to prove he's worth every bit of the £65m Villa paid to sign him from Chelsea

articles.title: Career gone wrong? Ex-Germany player in the Regionalliga at 30
articles.summary: We can probably all still remember Max Meyer. More precisely, how he was predicted to have a great career and outstanding potential. And what became of it: n...
articles.body:
We can probably all still remember Max Meyer. More precisely, how he was predicted to have a great career and outstanding potential. And what became of it: not all that much.

Now, one of the biggest "what if" careers seems to be coming to an end on football's big stage. As 'Sky' and 'Reviersport' report, Meyer is stepping away from the professional game at just 30 and will play in the Regionalliga West for Rot-Weiß Oberhausen in the future.

Most recently, he spent two years under contract with APOEL Nicosia, where his deal expired this summer. In a way, the circle is now complete: the central midfielder grew up in Oberhausen and already played there in his youth.

He made his breakthrough at Schalke 04 after a stop in Duisburg. Back then, he became a DFB player. He left the Royal Blues on a free transfer for Crystal Palace in 2018 after he and the Ruhr club were unable to agree on a contract extension.

The fact that his advisor at the time described him as a "world-class player" followed him every step of the way in the years that followed, though not in a positive sense. Expectations and reality, potential and actual achievement, never really matched up in Meyer's career.

After three years at Palace, he had a brief spell at 1. FC Köln before heading abroad again: he turned out for Fenerbahçe, Midtjylland and FC Luzern.

So now it appears to be the end of his professional football career. A player who once became U21 European champion and was considered one of Germany's great hopes is turning his back on the big stage. He is expected to sign a two-year contract with Oberhausen. His medical is scheduled for today, Monday.

Was Meyer's departure from Schalke, perceived by some as arrogant, the knockout blow for his career? Or was he simply overhyped from the start? Write it in the comments!

articles.title: Robinson's rhythmical action reminiscent of McGrath - Agnew
articles.summary: Glenn McGrath-like Ollie Robinson has Australia to thank for bringing back into fashion an age-old tactic which is fuelling his success.
articles.body:
After Ollie Robinson's England debut five years ago I said he was the most natural bowler I have seen.

A lot has gone under the bridge since – he was dropped, recalled, dropped again and is now back - but nothing has changed my mind on that.

Using the word robotic to describe him may give the wrong impression. It is a compliment.

Australia's great bowler Glenn McGrath was like that. Everything was utterly rhythmical, repetitive and perfectly grooved.

As a former bowler I watch and see he has inherent rhythm and such a beautiful action. His wrist is just perfect.

Yes, the conditions this summer, in which he has now taken 23 wickets in three matches after England's win in the second Test at Lord's, have been perfect. Robinson would carry them around in his cricket bag if he could.

But the 32-year-old has performed magnificently in them.

Whatever he has wanted the ball to do – to swing in or out or to wobble off the seam – it has done.

He has not needed to go searching for wickets, instead just letting the ball flow naturally from his fingertips.

He will feel like he could take wickets running in blindfolded. There is no better feeling.

Another thing I admire in Robinson is that he is a really good reader of the game.

Tactically, he is extremely sharp. He can spot a batsman's weakness and interpret that into what it means for his own plans very quickly.

A coach told me when he first came into the side that he was a bowler who would give talks to his team-mates about how to get batsmen out even then.

It all adds to what makes him such a good bowler.

Many people will say Robinson's performances this summer show Ben Stokes, Brendon McCullum and managing director Rob Key were wrong to leave him out of their Ashes squad last winter.

Amid talk of a breakdown in trust between Robinson and the Stokes-McCullum regime, they prioritised bowlers with greater pace.

He probably has lost his way with his fitness at different times but I also think back to bowling coach Jon Lewis calling out his fitness in 2022.

There are times Robinson has not been handled as kindly as he might have been.

Perhaps last winter's omission focused his mind, allowing Joe Root to now reap the rewards.

Robinson can also thank Australia for bringing back into the fashion the age-old tactic of the wicketkeeper standing up to the stumps to pace bowlers.

Alex Carey did it so effectively during the Ashes and England are now copying with Robinson.

It may seem obvious but that tweak is really playing into Robinson's strengths.

If the wicketkeeper was stood back the modern batsman would be walking down the pitch to Robinson. With Jamie Smith up they can't because of the risk of being stumped.

It means Robinson can bowl a yard fuller, giving his deliveries more time to swing through the air and means more of Robinson's deliveries would hit the stumps rather than bouncing over from a shorter length.

Of course, you cannot do any of this without a good wicketkeeper. Praise must also go to Jamie Smith.

After we saw Smith struggle badly through the Ashes, he has clearly improved his glovework. Wicketkeeping coach Sarah Taylor has been working him hard before play with a drill where she whacks tennis balls towards him with a racket.

The ball skids through and, with a batsman stood in front edging, missing and hitting the ball, Smith has to stay low and take them.

Now the next question for Robinson is whether he can repeat this success on harder, flatter pitches, or in hot conditions which will test those fitness levels. England will face them in their three-Test series in South Africa this winter.

They have often left Robinson out for Test on more batter-friendly pitches but it is time for them to throw him in. He has earned that right.

England are working behind the scenes to get Robinson into the position where he maintains his pace around 82mph, rather than his current place of starting there before dropping to 77 or 78mph.

If he does that, the extra bounce he will get as a result should negate the loss of movement.

And before then I desperately hope England do not rest Robinson, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson or Josh Tongue for the third Test in Edgbaston.

England's new quartet has shown real promise. They may not have a frontline spinner but Robinson, who conceded runs at just 1.29 per over across the Lord's Test, can effectively do the holding job of a slow bowler if needed.

After their poor run England just need to keep on winning matches and, just as importantly, this group needs to get used to bowling together as an attack.

Joe Root must also learn how to use each of them best.

This, with Robinson as the leader, is England's best attack. Stick with it in Birmingham and beyond.

Jonathan Agnew was speaking to BBC Sport's Matthew Henry

articles.title: Ja Morant Sells Memphis Mansion For $3.2 Million Following Trail Blazers Move
articles.summary: Ja Morant has sold his seven-bedroom mansion in Memphis, Tennessee shortly after his move to the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers star Ja Morant has officially put his Memphis days behind him, as he no longer has a home in the city where he was drafted. The former Grizzlies player sold his two-story mansion in Memphis, Tennessee, for a reported amount of $3.2 million earlier this week after initially listing it for $3.5 million.

He initially paid $3.05 million for the mansion and has since made a $150,000 profit on the sale four years after buying it in 2022, when he signed his $197.2 million max contract with the Grizzlies. The house reportedly has seven bedrooms and spans 13,836 square feet on 6.45 acres.

'Homes of Celebs' got an inside look at the property. They described that it has a beautiful foyer, a home office, a living room with a built-in bar, a formal dining room, a kitchen, a private lounge, an en-suite bathroom, walk-in closets, a salon, a poker room, a billiards room, a sauna, a movie theater, and much more .

This property is apparently just 62 feet away from a property that he bought for his parents with his first contract in 2019. Morant reportedly has a net worth of $50 million and has already earned about $150 million through 2026 of his $236.8 million in guaranteed career earnings (leaving almost $87 million in future earnings over the next two years).

Former NBA Players Expect Ja Morant Will Bounce Back In 2026-27

The 27-year-old begins a new life in Portland with the Trail Blazers, now looking to bounce back from a controversy-ridden 2025-26 season in Memphis. Former NBA players Isaiah Thomas , Matt Barnes , and Stephen Jackson feel all eyes will be on Ja Morant in 2026-27 for a comeback season.

"Ja Morant is going to have a special season!! Pulling for bro frfr 🏁🏁🏁," wrote Thomas on X.

Stephen Jackson and Matt Barnes recorded an episode of the 'All the Smoke' podcast where they expressed their expectations for Morant in 2026-27.

"I'm happy for him. I f–ked up a million times and kept getting chances. So, I'm glad he understands. Well, I want him to understand that it's not what you do, it's what you do after. You got the opportunity to fix all this s–t by coming out averaging 18-20, having a great year," Stephen Jackson said.

"You're already doing great selling shoes. So, just come out and play basketball. Hope he's focused on just getting back to playing basketball because he has a great opportunity to play along. Dame and some other young stars," he added.

"If he comes out this year and averages 18 to 20, he doesn't really have the pressure because you got Dame there. You got Avdija who's really their number one option. You just come out and get back to doing what you love and having fun. You know, you get out of Memphis; this is a great opportunity to kind of reclaim who you are," he further added.

"They had expectations in Memphis with the team they had. It ain't nothing in Portland right now. No. So maybe this could help them get back and play freely again," Jackson said in his final thoughts on Morant's season. "Just hoop, just hoop," Barnes concluded.

Ja Morant is ready to enter the next chapter of his career and is fired up to play alongside Damian Lillard . He seems to be in a situation where he could have a lot more freedom and a lot less pressure of being the primary scorer every night, as he had with the Grizzlies. It will be very fascinating to see how things turn out for him in Portland.

articles.title: ‘Best signing by an absolute mile’: Neville lavishes praise on Man Utd game-changer after five-star display
articles.summary: Gary Neville couldn’t speak highly enough of Bruno Fernandes following the midfielder’s five-star display against Ipswich Town.The Manchester United skipper...
articles.body:
Gary Neville couldn't speak highly enough of Bruno Fernandes following the midfielder's five-star display against Ipswich Town.

The Manchester United skipper notched a hat-trick to help cement a much-needed 5-2 victory over Ipswich in gameweek two.

What did Neville have to say about Fernandes?

Fernandes' efforts were paramount to United bouncing back from their dismal opening-day defeat to Hull City, and the Reds now have their first win on the board in 2026/2027.

Reacting at full-time on Sky Sports, Neville said: "He (Fernandes) is exceptional. He's the best United signing in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era by an absolute mile.

"I think the biggest accolade that you can get in football is being voted the PFA Player of the Year, because that's your fellow professionals, and it's hard to get the opposition's dressing room to vote for you.

"I don't think the criticism's been there against him in the last 12-18 months. I think, to be fair, he's ridden that period where he did sometimes get a bit frustrated or he reacted [badly] as a captain. He's completely changed.

"He's matured. He's now got the respect of his professionals, to the point where they're voting him the PFA Player of the Year. He's exceptional in the sense that he takes risks, he passes forward, [and] he always looks to impact the game positively."

POTY Fernandes aiming for full-team triumphs rather than just personal

Fernandes winning the prestigious PFA award came on the back of his record-breaking season in 2025/2026, which ended with him setting a new Premier League assist record of 21 in a single term.

While such accolades emphasise his status as one of the world's best, the 31-year-old will have his heart set on securing team glory this campaign by winning some silverware.

articles.title: 'I was paralysed - now I'm running 5,000km'
articles.summary: Esmee Gummer is hosting a 5km run club in every British city and running between each location.
articles.body:
Esmee Gummer dreamed of becoming a professional dancer. At 18, and just six weeks before she was due to start dance college, complications following surgery left her paralysed from the waist down and unsure if she would ever walk again.

Now 35, she has swapped life at her home in Hackney, east London, for a campervan as she attempts to run 5,000km (3,107 miles) around the UK and Ireland.

She is leading a free 5km (3.1 mile) run club in every British city, as well as Dublin, as part of her project – The Nation's 5k – to inspire people to "say yes to movement before it's too late".

Since setting off from Inverness in June, she has consumed countless carbohydrate gels and worn out at least five pairs of trainers.

A support crew drives the van between cities, but Gummer, originally from Heybridge, Essex, is making the journey on foot, running for up to seven hours a day as she aims to complete the challenge in 99 days.

Gummer has ticked off more than 50 cities so far and says she has received a warm welcome everywhere she has been.

A large crowd turned out to welcome her back to her home county when she arrived in Colchester.

"People were coming along because they were like, 'She's from Essex and we've got to do this with her,' so for sure I felt the difference with how people showed up and just how amazing everybody was," she says.

Some of her longest days will involve running up to 70km (43.5 miles), about the same as running from the Royal Albert Hall in London to the beach in Southend-on-Sea.

Each day, she enjoys a few hours of recovery before lacing up her trainers once again to lead a run club in the evening, which she says is often attended by hundreds of runners.

Several running clubs attended the session in Colchester's Castle Park, including about 40 members of Run Like A Girl Colchester.

"We'd have regretted it if we didn't go," says the club's founder Mathilda Coldwell. "It was really nice vibes."

Some runners have even gone to multiple cities to support Gummer's challenge.

Gary Parr, from Cambridgeshire, joined the runs in all three of the county's cities – Cambridge, Ely, and Peterborough – and hopes to travel to London for the final day of the challenge on 3 October.

"I'm absolutely in awe of everything she's doing," he says.

Gummer has dedicated most of her adult life to encouraging people to find joy in movement. She started studying to become a personal trainer about a year after she learnt to walk again and has worked in the fitness industry ever since.

The challenge is a fundraiser for the charities Wings for Life and Sport in Mind, and Gummer will be making donations to organisations nominated by people in each city she visits.

"What's been so special about [The Nation's 5k] is it's given people a purpose," she says.

"I just can't believe it when I find out that people from up north are booking Airbnbs for 3 October to be in London. It's going to take a while to really settle in that people have gone out of their way to do that."

Asked what she would say to her teenage self, she responds: "I do remember at the time thinking I don't ever want to work this hard again in case I lose it because it hurt so much.

"I think now, 18-year-old me would look at this moment and go, 'Thank you, because you've tried again,' and I think that finish line at the end is for my 18-year-old self to say, 'I want to prove to you that it doesn't always go wrong if you work hard'."
